**Pages:** conservative-finite-volume-weak-limits / conservative-finite-volume-weak-limits-examples.

**Scope:** Define cell averages and a conservative consistent numerical-flux update for u_t+f(u)_x=0. # Independent numerical ODE prerequisite pairs — intake proposal

Draft proposal only. No ML consumer is a prerequisite. All procedures and proofs remain to be authored.

### P-NUM-ODE-01 — One-step ODE consistency and local error

**Pages:** one-step-ode-consistency-and-local-error / one-step-ode-consistency-and-local-error-examples. **Scope:** Define a one-step method $\Psi_h(t,y)$, local defect $\|\Psi_h(t,y(t))-y(t+h)\|$, and stability. For a fixed interval $[0,T]$ and exact solutions staying in a compact tube, state the order-$p$ hypothesis as a uniform local defect $\le Ch^{p+1}$ and the one-step stability bound $\|\Psi_h(t,u)-\Psi_h(t,v)\|\le(1+Lh)\|u-v\|$. Derive these premises for Euler when $f$ is $C^1$ in time and state with bounded derivatives on that tube; any named Runge–Kutta method must state its order conditions and required derivatives separately. **Proof route:** Taylor-expand the exact flow and the selected method increment, bound remainders uniformly on the tube, and prove the stated stability estimate; do not infer an order from the method label alone. **Examples:** Euler on a scalar linear field; a nonsmooth field where its local order drops. **Requires:** thm-existence-and-uniqueness-of-a-maximal-ode-solution, thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives, and a proved Taylor remainder estimate; the local error calculation is explicit, but a numerical-analysis source remains unaudited. **Sources:** Chen et al., neural-ODE Appendix B/C and numerical issues, PDF pp. 13–16, and Papamakarios et al., continuous-flow section pp. 31–33, discuss solver use but do not prove the error theorem. Acquire/read a matching numerical-ODE source before publication. This pair precedes P-NUM-ODE-02.

### P-NUM-ODE-02 — Global ODE and log-density integration error

**Pages:** global-ode-and-density-error / global-ode-and-density-error-examples. **Scope:** Under P-NUM-ODE-01’s uniform order-$p$ defect/stability bounds and a fixed finite interval, derive $\max_n\|y_n-y(t_n)\|\le C_T h^p$ by the discrete Grönwall recurrence. For a continuous normalizing flow augment the state by $\ell'=-\operatorname{div}f(x,t)$ and bound the log-density error separately. For Euler, $f\in C^2$ with bounded derivatives on a compact tube makes the augmented vector field locally Lipschitz and supports a local $O(h^2)$ defect; for order $p>1$, require the method-specific order conditions and enough bounded derivatives of the augmented field, or state a separate quadrature theorem with matching smoothness. $C^2$ regularity alone does not justify arbitrary order-$p$ convergence. State solver, quadrature, and state-error contributions separately. A state trajectory error alone does not control log-density or adjoint-gradient error. **Proof route:** derive $e_{n+1}\le(1+Lh)e_n+Ch^{p+1}$, iterate it, then apply a second bound to the augmented/log-density component under its own local defect and stability estimates. **Examples:** Euler global error for a linear flow; same state solver with a separately refined density quadrature. **Requires:** P-NUM-ODE-01 — One-step ODE consistency and local error; discrete Grönwall and the divergence-Lipschitz estimate, proved locally if no exact supplier exists. **Sources:** Chen et al. pp. 13–16 and Papamakarios et al. pp. 31–33 discuss solver use and numerical issues but do not prove these error theorems; the local defect/stability/Grönwall proof remains a clearly specified authoring obligation. ML-58 — Neural ODEs and continuous normalizing flows and ML-61 — Conditional flow matching and transport paths consume this only when numerical error is claimed.


## Binding consumed contract

**P-NUM-ODE-01/02.** Fix d≥1, T>0, h=T/N, N≥1, a common open time-state domain and a compact solution tube with positive margin. Use Euclidean vector norms and induced operator norms. The exact IVP solution y and every numerical stage/state in the theorem stay in that tube. A one-step map Ψ_h(t,·) is defined there and satisfies, for constants C,L≥0 independent of N and j, ||Ψ_h(t_j,y(t_j))−y(t_(j+1))||≤C h^(p+1) and ||Ψ_h(t_j,v)−Ψ_h(t_j,w)||≤(1+Lh)||v−w||. With initial error e₀≤C₀h^p, prove max_j e_j≤(C₀e^(LT)+C(e^(LT)−1)/L)h^p for L>0, and (C₀+CT)h^p for L=0. Derive Euler's C and L from f∈C¹ with finite field, time-derivative and state-Jacobian bounds on the tube; derive each higher-order tableau's defect separately from its exact derivative/order conditions. For augmented log density ℓ′=−div f, Euler requires f∈C² with bounded relevant derivatives of f and div f, the augmented tube, and a separate state/log-defect estimate; no arbitrary higher order follows from C². Local proof route: Taylor/integral remainder, invariant-tube admissibility and geometric-sum recurrence, using actual root ODE/Taylor/Grönwall suppliers. Matching source design: Hairer–Wanner Ch. III §§III.2–III.5, PDF pp. 4–11/printed 60–67, as recorded by the recovery packet. NA-15 supplies concrete conditions to instantiate the abstract theorem, never a prerequisite of the generic theorem. Consumers: NA-15, NA-18 notation only, NA-21 when numerical shooting is quantified, NA-45 matching ODE terms.


The abstract recurrence/global-error theorem is owned by P-NUM-ODE-02; P-NUM-ODE-01 owns local defect/stability definitions and Euler derivation. NA-15 owns concrete higher-order tableaux. The recurrence accepts hypotheses directly and must never depend back on NA-15.

## XA-01 — extend canonical rare-event/SMC guarantees; do not duplicate algorithms

**Existing home:** `library/bayesian-computational-statistics/feynman-kac-particle-filters.md` and its examples. Existing `alg-sequential-importance-resampling`, `alg-multinomial-and-residual-offspring-resampling`, `thm-sequential-particle-estimator-is-unbiased`, `lem-feynman-kac-path-measures-satisfy-forward-recursion` retain their homes. Existing IS unbiasedness, finite variance and CLT are already covered; no new IS pair.

**New delta.** Integration owner: optimization/statistics RARE1 absorbs this amendment; no separate pair or competing procedure. Define a finite sequence of nested events/levels with exact stopped transition kernels and potentials 0≤G≤1. Prove measurability of finite-budget stopped kernels (or a declared exact-hitting oracle), connection of their Feynman–Kac normalizer to the target event probability, and error of any time-discretized crossing approximation separately. Use existing SMC product-normalizer estimator; its unbiasedness is reused only under all positive-prefix-normalizer/full-resampling hypotheses. Then prove a finite-horizon L2 bound with explicit dependence on number of levels, prefix probabilities, bounded normalized potentials and kernel mixing. A safe first contract is an O(1/N) **absolute** mean-square bound for a fixed number of bounded-potential levels, proved by conditional variance and induction. Relative error divides by the squared rare probability and may be huge. An efficiency claim uniform in rarity needs an additional theorem and actual lower bounds/minorization; not “splitting reduces variance” by name.

**Missing local suppliers / owner.** Local to this amendment: stopped-kernel construction and cemetery handling; Feynman–Kac event identity; conditional empirical variance identity for the actual resampling procedure; finite-level martingale/variance recursion; bias from approximate crossing/hitting kernels. Existing finite-horizon SMC unbiasedness does not by itself imply finite-particle accuracy or uniform-in-time stability (the canonical page explicitly says so). No adaptive-level unbiasedness without its separate order-statistic/martingale proof. Root must assign this amendment to the statistics guarantee owner and check affected consumers if an existing statement changes; prefer new theorem carriers without altering original definitions.

**Examples.** Reliability chain crossing; extinction estimate; all particles die (zero estimate, not algorithmic proof of zero probability); an IS proposal with infinite weighted second moment; same budget splitting with worse relative error. **Sources:** Cérou–Del Moral–Furon–Guyader, “Sequential Monte Carlo for rare event estimation,” Statistics and Computing 22 (2012), pp. 795–808, DOI `10.1007/s11222-011-9231-6`; Del Moral, *Feynman–Kac Formulae* (2004), particle variance/martingale chapters, DOI `10.1007/978-1-4684-9393-1`. Exact source hypotheses are intake obligations.

source_record_verbatim.promise_and_proof_design_verbatim: **A scope.** Scalar Brownian Milstein Y_(n+1)=Y_n+b(Y_n)h+sigma(Y_n)DeltaW+0.5 sigma sigma'(Y_n)((DeltaW)^2-h). Under globally Lipschitz b,sigma and sufficient bounded/Lipschitz derivatives (state explicitly C_b^3 suffices with finite initial moments), prove grid RMS order1. Multidimensional commutative noise extension after proving L_i sigma_j=L_j sigma_i yields symmetrized iterated integrals; noncommuting noise requires Levy areas with their own sampling approximation error and cost. Also supply scalar additive-noise stochastic Heun: Z=Y+b(Y)h+sigma DeltaW, Ynew=Y+0.5h[b(Y)+b(Z)]+sigma DeltaW, constant sigma. Prove weak order2 for b in C_b^6 and payoff backward solution with the actual mixed derivatives through spatial order6/time order3 bounded, by one-step moment matching through h² and O(h³) remainder. This specific weak2 guarantee does not extend to multiplicative noise without extra terms. New Milstein MLMC delta: nested commutative-Milstein paths have E|Yfine-Ycoarse|²=O(h²), hence Lipschitz payoff variance O(h²); with cost O(h^-1) and bias O(h) consume canonical MLMC theorem to obtain O(eps^-2). **Proof/prereqs:** same-pair iterated Itô integral identity I_11=((DeltaW)^2-h)/2, conditional moments/orthogonality, local mean O(h²), local RMS O(h^(3/2)) and stochastic stability recurrence proving global order1. General stochastic local-to-global theorem is authored here; existing deterministic theorem insufficient. **B:** geometric Brownian motion, scalar multiplicative noise, noncommuting two-noise area term. **Cost:** derivatives and Gaussian/area samples; arbitrary Levy areas not free. **Sources:** Kloeden/Platen, Numerical Solution of SDEs, Itô-Taylor and strong approximation chapters; Higham, SIAM Review 43 (2001), Milstein section. **Disposition:** extend-existing substantial algorithm/error guarantee. `ex-quantile-coupling-on-the-real-line` already proves generalized inverse Q(U) has the target law; `lem-randomized-probability-integral-transform` treats the reverse randomized CDF transform. Do not redefine those statistical transformations as a new method. The example is contextual rather than a legal logical supplier; consume `thm-probability-law-and-distribution-function-correspondence` and promote only the needed generalized-inverse sublevel identity to a typed prerequisite with proof/source attribution, avoiding a duplicate broad quantile-coupling theorem. The new guarantee is actual bit/stream implementation and finite-distribution error plus Box-Muller sampling, absent from inspected canonical methods.

**Randomness model:** independent ideal fair bits B_j on an explicitly constructed countable product probability space; U=sum B_j 2^-j has uniform law by dyadic cylinder intervals and continuity of measure. Disjoint bit blocks/streams preserve independence. A b-bit K uniform on {0,...,2^b-1} gives U_b=(K+1/2)2^-b, coupling |U-U_b|<=2^(-b-1), hence W1 at most that and Kolmogorov discrepancy at most 2^-b. Finite-support versus continuous law has total variation distance1, so no TV-small assertion. Independence of finite outputs requires disjoint independent bit blocks; recycling bits changes dependence.

**Practical finite generators:** define an actual full-period LCG modulo 2^w with odd increment and multiplier a congruent1 mod4, w>=2; prove full period by induction modulo powers of2 using affine iterate arithmetic, and state finite state/period bound for every deterministic generator. With random uniform initial state each single state is uniform, but adjacent states satisfy the recurrence and are not independent. Give a counter-based stream interface as a deterministic keyed permutation of finite counters; a random permutation/key model or computational pseudorandomness assumption must be explicit, never an IID theorem. No cryptographic-quality claim or empirical-test proof of independence. Non-overlapping blocks avoid exact reuse only within certified period; do not imply probabilistic independence.

**Variates:** inverse CDF already canonical; add implemented bracketed inverse with certified |F(xhat)-u|<=epsilon on a monotone continuous CDF, finite-bit U discrepancy adds to Kolmogorov error (plus any actual CDF approximation error). Spatial error requires density f>=m>0 on the inversion bracket, and tails handled separately. Discrete CDF binary search gives exact categorical law under ideal U, finite-bit count discrepancy bounded per threshold; Bernoulli rational sampling via unbiased integer rejection has geometric expected bit/block cost and budget failure; finite budget discarded separately.

Box-Muller uses independent ideal U1,U2 in (0,1), Z1=sqrt(-2 log U1)cos(2pi U2), Z2=sqrt(-2 log U1)sin(2pi U2). Prove independent standard-normal density by polar change of variables and product density normalization; same-pair polar Jacobian/measure change prerequisite must be proved if not published. Finite bits imply bounded normal tails and discrete output, never exact Gaussian; couple midpoint U_b to U, restrict U1>=delta and guard angular/endpoint arithmetic, derivative bounds give explicit Wasserstein/bounded-Lipschitz output error on that event, while discarded event probability <=delta+2^-b. Tail expectations use proved Gaussian/Rayleigh moments and Cauchy-Schwarz; elementary log/sqrt/trig evaluation errors supplied by precision owner add through those derivative bounds. No Ziggurat implementation required if not fully specified/proved; rejection algorithm may be a later optional genuinely new optimization only with envelope/area proof. Gaussian samples in SDE algorithms are ideal-law or approximate-law with this additional coupling error propagated; no invisible exact-normal finite-bit oracle.

**Same-frontier prerequisites:** product independent-bit construction (reuse existing countable product theorem if available, otherwise own cylinder extension), dyadic uniform law, LCG modular induction, stopping/rejection cost, finite-CDF inverse residual, polar transform identity, truncated-transform coupling and arithmetic error propagation. Root must map any newly located canonical supplier instead of creating duplicate items. **Examples:** low-bit LCG correlation/lattice, normal tail truncation, zero endpoint log failure, inverse CDF near vanishing density. **Cost:** random bits, rejection count, integer arithmetic, precision and transform calls; bit cost distinct from real-RAM sampling oracle cost. **Sources, unread candidates:** Devroye, Non-Uniform Random Variate Generation, author's full-book portal https://luc.devroye.org/rnbookindex.html ; L'Ecuyer RNG publications https://www.iro.umontreal.ca/~lecuyer/myftp/papers.html ; Box/Muller, Ann Math Stat 29 (1958), https://doi.org/10.1214/aoms/1177706645 . Canonical quantile source https://sites.math.duke.edu/~rtd/PTE/PTE5_011119.pdf .

### NA-04 — Stationary iterations and relaxation

**Pages:** stationary-iterations-and-relaxation / stationary-iterations-and-relaxation-examples.

**Scope:** Define a matrix splitting A=M−N and the stationary update x_{j+1}=M^-1Nx_j+M^-1b; supply Richardson, Jacobi, Gauss–Seidel, and SOR as exact algorithms with their admissible diagonal/pivot rules. State the all-start/all-right-hand-side convergence equivalence ρ(M^-1N)<1. Prove only the source-backed sufficient tests: strict diagonal dominance, or irreducible weak diagonal dominance with at least one strict row, for Jacobi/Gauss–Seidel; for symmetric A with positive diagonal, SOR converges for every start iff A is positive definite and 0<ω<2. Keep ordering assumptions on any optimal-ω formula.

**Proof route:** Reduce the error to G^j e_0; use Jordan form/spectral radius for the all-start equivalence and norm contraction only as a sufficient condition. Explicitly permit transient nonnormal growth and polynomial factors from defective dominant roots. Prove named matrix-class criteria separately from the general theorem.

**Examples:** diagonally dominant Jacobi; SPD SOR for 0<ω<2; a splitting with ρ(G)≥1 and an initial error that misses the unstable eigenspace.

**Requires:** NA-03; published Linear Algebra pages krylov-subspaces-arnoldi-and-gmres and matrix-norms-condition-numbers-and-numerical-stability, including def-stationary-iteration-from-a-matrix-splitting and thm-stationary-splitting-converges-iff-the-iteration-matrix-has-spectral-radius-below-one.

**Sources:** Saad Ch. 4 §§4.1–4.2, printed pp. 105–126, read in full; Cornell lecture 31 complete PDF; URLs as in NA-03 and exact read records in iterative/sources.json. Convergence factors do not follow from a method name.

These are preservation/completion clauses, not permission to erase approved claims.

### NA-45 — Error budgets for computational inference

**Pages:** error-budgets-for-computational-inference / error-budgets-for-computational-inference-examples.

**Scope:** Define a target-to-computation path for an integral, likelihood, or SDE expectation and prove a pathwise triangle-inequality decomposition into deterministic quadrature/discretization, algebraic solve/optimization residual, finite-precision, Monte Carlo/randomization, approximation, data-sampling, and model error where each term is defined. State that some terms may be random and need their own mode (pathwise, in expectation, or probability). Root-sum-square requires covariance/independence premises. A solver rate that vanishes under refinement does not remove a fixed model/score bias. This page supplies numerical bookkeeping, not posterior calibration or inferential coverage.

**Proof route:** Insert intermediate exact targets and apply the triangle inequality along the computation path. For randomized terms, derive a variance sum only after proving centering and cross-covariance conditions; keep deterministic truncation/conditioning terms separate. Reuse P-NUM-ODE/SDE only for their exact solver contracts and do not infer model correctness.

**Examples:** quadrature plus optimizer residual in a likelihood normalizer; MC standard error shrinking while SDE time-discretization bias remains; numerical refinement with a nonzero learned-model bias.

**Requires:** NA-01, NA-12, NA-13, NA-14, NA-39, NA-40, NA-41, NA-42, NA-43, and NA-44; independent planned P-NUM-ODE-01/02 and P-NUM-SDE-01/02 only for the matching solver terms.

**Sources:** Owen, Simple Monte Carlo Ch. 2 §§2.1–2.3 and 2.9, printed pp. 15–21 and 35–36 / PDF pp. 16–22 and 36–37, selected sections read: https://artowen.su.domains/mc/Ch-intro.pdf; Practical QMC Chs. 15 and 17, complete main text/notes/exercises read at PDF pp. 11–72 and 103–160: https://artowen.su.domains/mc/practicalqmc.pdf; Giles, full §3 Theorem 3.1 and proof, PDF pp. 1–11: https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/gilesm/files/OPRE_2008.pdf; Higham–Mao–Stuart, journal pp. 1041–1056 / PDF pp. 1–16 read, later pp. 1057–1063 unread: https://authors.library.caltech.edu/records/1wrtf-vyz04/files/s0036142901389530.pdf; Boyd–Vandenberghe §§9.2, 9.3.1 and 9.5.1–9.5.3 read at physical PDF pp. 477–483 and 498–506: https://web.stanford.edu/~boyd/cvxbook/bv_cvxbook.pdf; Hansen, Ch. 4 all 29 slides, Ch. 5 all 27 slides, and Ch. 3 pp. 1–6 read: https://www2.imm.dtu.dk/~pcha/DIP/. # Independent numerical ODE prerequisite pairs — intake proposal

Draft proposal only. No ML consumer is a prerequisite. All procedures and proofs remain to be authored.

### P-NUM-ODE-01 — One-step ODE consistency and local error

**Pages:** one-step-ode-consistency-and-local-error / one-step-ode-consistency-and-local-error-examples. **Scope:** Define a one-step method $\Psi_h(t,y)$, local defect $\|\Psi_h(t,y(t))-y(t+h)\|$, and stability. For a fixed interval $[0,T]$ and exact solutions staying in a compact tube, state the order-$p$ hypothesis as a uniform local defect $\le Ch^{p+1}$ and the one-step stability bound $\|\Psi_h(t,u)-\Psi_h(t,v)\|\le(1+Lh)\|u-v\|$. Derive these premises for Euler when $f$ is $C^1$ in time and state with bounded derivatives on that tube; any named Runge–Kutta method must state its order conditions and required derivatives separately. **Proof route:** Taylor-expand the exact flow and the selected method increment, bound remainders uniformly on the tube, and prove the stated stability estimate; do not infer an order from the method label alone. **Examples:** Euler on a scalar linear field; a nonsmooth field where its local order drops. **Requires:** thm-existence-and-uniqueness-of-a-maximal-ode-solution, thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives, and a proved Taylor remainder estimate; the local error calculation is explicit, but a numerical-analysis source remains unaudited. **Sources:** Chen et al., neural-ODE Appendix B/C and numerical issues, PDF pp. 13–16, and Papamakarios et al., continuous-flow section pp. 31–33, discuss solver use but do not prove the error theorem. Acquire/read a matching numerical-ODE source before publication. This pair precedes P-NUM-ODE-02.

### P-NUM-ODE-02 — Global ODE and log-density integration error

**Pages:** global-ode-and-density-error / global-ode-and-density-error-examples. **Scope:** Under P-NUM-ODE-01’s uniform order-$p$ defect/stability bounds and a fixed finite interval, derive $\max_n\|y_n-y(t_n)\|\le C_T h^p$ by the discrete Grönwall recurrence. For a continuous normalizing flow augment the state by $\ell'=-\operatorname{div}f(x,t)$ and bound the log-density error separately. For Euler, $f\in C^2$ with bounded derivatives on a compact tube makes the augmented vector field locally Lipschitz and supports a local $O(h^2)$ defect; for order $p>1$, require the method-specific order conditions and enough bounded derivatives of the augmented field, or state a separate quadrature theorem with matching smoothness. $C^2$ regularity alone does not justify arbitrary order-$p$ convergence. State solver, quadrature, and state-error contributions separately. A state trajectory error alone does not control log-density or adjoint-gradient error. **Proof route:** derive $e_{n+1}\le(1+Lh)e_n+Ch^{p+1}$, iterate it, then apply a second bound to the augmented/log-density component under its own local defect and stability estimates. **Examples:** Euler global error for a linear flow; same state solver with a separately refined density quadrature. **Requires:** P-NUM-ODE-01 — One-step ODE consistency and local error; discrete Grönwall and the divergence-Lipschitz estimate, proved locally if no exact supplier exists. **Sources:** Chen et al. pp. 13–16 and Papamakarios et al. pp. 31–33 discuss solver use and numerical issues but do not prove these error theorems; the local defect/stability/Grönwall proof remains a clearly specified authoring obligation. ML-58 — Neural ODEs and continuous normalizing flows and ML-61 — Conditional flow matching and transport paths consume this only when numerical error is claimed.


## Binding consumed contract

**P-NUM-ODE-01/02.** Fix d≥1, T>0, h=T/N, N≥1, a common open time-state domain and a compact solution tube with positive margin. Use Euclidean vector norms and induced operator norms. The exact IVP solution y and every numerical stage/state in the theorem stay in that tube. A one-step map Ψ_h(t,·) is defined there and satisfies, for constants C,L≥0 independent of N and j, ||Ψ_h(t_j,y(t_j))−y(t_(j+1))||≤C h^(p+1) and ||Ψ_h(t_j,v)−Ψ_h(t_j,w)||≤(1+Lh)||v−w||. With initial error e₀≤C₀h^p, prove max_j e_j≤(C₀e^(LT)+C(e^(LT)−1)/L)h^p for L>0, and (C₀+CT)h^p for L=0. Derive Euler's C and L from f∈C¹ with finite field, time-derivative and state-Jacobian bounds on the tube; derive each higher-order tableau's defect separately from its exact derivative/order conditions. For augmented log density ℓ′=−div f, Euler requires f∈C² with bounded relevant derivatives of f and div f, the augmented tube, and a separate state/log-defect estimate; no arbitrary higher order follows from C². Local proof route: Taylor/integral remainder, invariant-tube admissibility and geometric-sum recurrence, using actual root ODE/Taylor/Grönwall suppliers. Matching source design: Hairer–Wanner Ch. III §§III.2–III.5, PDF pp. 4–11/printed 60–67, as recorded by the recovery packet. NA-15 supplies concrete conditions to instantiate the abstract theorem, never a prerequisite of the generic theorem. Consumers: NA-15, NA-18 notation only, NA-21 when numerical shooting is quantified, NA-45 matching ODE terms.


The abstract recurrence/global-error theorem is owned by P-NUM-ODE-02; P-NUM-ODE-01 owns local defect/stability definitions and Euler derivation. NA-15 owns concrete higher-order tableaux. The recurrence accepts hypotheses directly and must never depend back on NA-15.

source_record_verbatim.title: Riemann solvers for hyperbolic systems
source_record_verbatim.scope: For f in C3 on an open admissible set G in Rm, define strictly hyperbolic conservation systems and admissible-state set, characteristic families, Rankine–Hugoniot and Lax admissibility as definitions. Prove the local small-data Riemann solver near a state where each field is genuinely nonlinear or linearly degenerate, with clearly bounded neighborhood; do not promise arbitrary large-data solutions. Define Godunov, Roe and HLL fluxes. Prove consistency and conservation; Roe property is an algebraic identity, not entropy admissibility. For ideal-gas Euler define pressure mathematically on rho>0, E>|m|²/(2rho), derive eigenstructure and give admissibility/failure conditions; HLL wave-speed bounds are explicit hypotheses or separately proved bounds.
source_record_verbatim.proof_route: Prove eigenpair smoothness under simple spectrum, local rarefaction integral curves, shock curves using an augmented Rankine–Hugoniot implicit-function argument, tangent matching and wave-composition invertibility; verify weak jumps. Prove HLL flux by integrating the two-wave approximate conservation balance. Derive Euler sound speed and contact eigenvector locally. source_record_verbatim.promise_and_proof_design_verbatim: **A scope.** Explicit Poisson tau leap Y_(n+1)=Y_n+sum nu_j P_j(a_j(Y_n)h), conditionally independent counts; prove weak order1 under bounded C^k globally extended propensities and smooth backward payoff solution with derivative bounds, or finite-state stopped model with exit error separately bounded. Couple levels by shared/minimum-intensity Poisson clocks; derive local discrepancy variance bound under explicit Lipschitz rates, propagate with jump martingale estimates before applying generic MLMC. Negative populations, unbounded rates and extinction are explicit failures of naive hypotheses. Give critical-reaction SSA/binomial guarded leap algorithm with finite budgets; do not transfer Poisson weak theorem unchanged. Chemical Langevin/diffusion scaling is a model approximation: for density X^V/V with jump nu/V and rates V a(x), generator Taylor gives O(1/V²) third-order remainder versus diffusion under smoothness and compact stopping, then a separate backward regularity argument bounds weak model error on finite T. This is not time-discretization error. **Proof/prereqs:** T16 martingale coupling and generator Dynkin identity; same-pair discrete weak telescoping, moments and stopped exit probability. **B:** death reaction negative counts, stiff reversible reactions, diffusion wrong near extinction, coupled tau-leap. **Cost:** R Poisson samples per leap vs event-count SSA; RNG cost/model and coupling work stated. **Sources:** Gillespie, J Chem Phys 115 (2001), tau leap; Anderson/Higham, Multiscale Modeling & Simulation 10 (2012), multilevel CTMC simulation; Kurtz diffusion approximation (full source selected/read before claiming functional limit). Reads pending.

## NA15 explicit extension — `TIME-SSP` owner and stabilized Chebyshev stepping

**Classification:** extend-existing, genuinely new time guarantees. Reuse canonical `def-chebyshev-polynomials-first-and-second-kind`, `thm-chebyshev-multiple-angle-identities`, `lem-chebyshev-degree-leading-coefficients-and-extreme-values`; do not reintroduce approximation polynomials.

**SSP method:** SSPRK(3,3): Y1=u+h f(u), Y2=3u/4+(Y1+h f(Y1))/4, unew=u/3+2(Y2+h f(Y2))/3. Prove third order by actual Taylor coefficients. If the forward Euler map preserves a specified convex invariant set C or satisfies a convex functional Phi(u+h f(u))<=Phi(u) for every u in C and 0<=h<=h_FE, convexity of C/Phi proves every stage and update preserve that property with coefficient1 and same timestep bound. State the premise at each stage and include boundary/time-dependent operators via augmented time or actual stage times. TVD is licensed only when the spatial forward-Euler theorem supplies Phi=TV and its CFL. No universal SSP claim for RK4. PDE PE04 consumes `TIME-SSP` = this NA15 proof interface. Missing lemma convex composition is owned NA15; no unowned key.

**Stabilized explicit method:** first order R_s(z)=T_s(1+z/s²), s>=1, implemented by y0=y, y1=y+(h/s²)Ay and yj=2 y_(j-1)-y_(j-2)+(2h/s²)A y_(j-1). For the second-order linear RKC variant s>=2, use w1=3/(s²-1), b=(s²-1)/(3s²), a=1-b and R_s(z)=a+b T_s(1+w1 z). Evaluate the same three-term Chebyshev recurrence with h/s² replaced by w1 h and output a y0+b ys. Prove T_s'(1)=s² and T_s''(1)=s²(s²-1)/3 by differentiating the recurrence; hence R(0)=R'(0)=R''(0)=1 and actual order2 on fixed linear autonomous systems. Stability intervals are [-2s²,0] for order1 and [-2(s²-1)/3,0] for order2 because |T_s(x)|<=1 on [-1,1] and 0<b<1. For self-adjoint nonpositive A in the declared inner product, spectral theorem gives contraction when h rho(-A) is within that interval. For nonsymmetric A eigenvalue inclusion alone is insufficient; require a proved functional calculus or bounded diagonalization constants. Inhomogeneous equations use an explicitly augmented system with forcing regularity or separate Duhamel discretization.

Use s~sqrt(h rho) stages and count s matrix-vector products, versus O(h rho) forward Euler substeps for the same macro h. This is a stability-work comparison, not an accuracy speedup theorem. Prove global fixed-T order from local Taylor remainder and stable propagation with explicit ||A³u|| bound; do not claim mesh-uniform order from bounded scalar R alone. Internal stage perturbations satisfy a forced Chebyshev recurrence; use U_j with |U_j(x)|<=j+1 to bound O(s² max perturbation) on the stable segment and include roundoff/action errors. Nonlinear RKC needs an actual nonlinear stage construction and order proof; this linear variant does not supply one silently. Examples: semidiscrete self-adjoint heat, stiff reaction negative spectrum, nonnormal failure, stage-roundoff growth. Source candidates (unread): https://www.unige.ch/~hairer/books.html ; https://doi.org/10.1137/S003614450036757X (SSP review locator, exact record to verify before binding); Sommeijer/Shampine/Verwer RKC algorithm via author portal https://homepages.cwi.nl/~verwer/ .

## NA15 nonlinear RKC construction (bind instead of stopping at linear example)

Preserve the simple linear proof above as the stability model, and include this actual autonomous nonlinear second-order stabilized explicit RK recurrence. For s>=2 set w1=3/(s²-1), b0=b1=b2=1/4 and b_j=(j²-1)/(3j²) for j>=2, a_j=1-b_j. Let Y0=y, Y1=y+b1 w1 h f(y). For j=2,...,s define mu_j=2 b_j/b_(j-1), nu_j=-b_j/b_(j-2), mt_j=2 b_j w1/b_(j-1), gt_j=-a_(j-1) mt_j, and

Yj=(1-mu_j-nu_j)y+mu_j Y_(j-1)+nu_j Y_(j-2)+mt_j h f(Y_(j-1))+gt_j h f(y).

Output Ys. It is an explicit RK method because every stage is an affine combination of y and earlier RHS evaluations. At constant f its stage abscissae follow c1=b1 w1 and c_j=b_j w1 j² for j>=2, hence c_s=1. Derive the coefficient of f'f by expanding the recurrence through h², or equivalently use the one order2 rooted tree plus actual scalar stability polynomial a_s+b_s T_s(1+w1 z), to prove final coefficient1/2. This equivalence is justified only through order2; higher-order linear matching does not establish nonlinear order. For f in C2 with bounded derivatives on a controlled tube and all stages admitted, Taylor remainder plus one-step Lipschitz propagation proves global order2 for fixed s on fixed T. The long real stability interval remains a scalar linear/normal-matrix guarantee; nonlinear dissipation, positivity, SSP and stiffness-uniform accuracy do not follow. Time-dependent f is handled by augmenting t'=1 and using the actual derived c_j, not an arbitrary stage-time guess. Include an explicit finite-stage domain check and s-dependent roundoff amplification. Damped w0>1 variants are optional only with separately verified coefficients; the undamped scheme already has the proved interval and actual nonlinear method.

**Scope:** Define a fixed-step k-step recurrence, generating polynomials ρ and σ, local truncation error from inserting the exact solution, consistency conditions ρ(1)=0 and ρ'(1)=σ(1), and order p. Define the root condition as roots in |ζ|≤1 with simple unit-modulus roots; repeated roots strictly inside are permitted. Prove equal-step convergence order p from consistency, root condition, O(h^p) starting values, a fixed solution tube, and a well-defined selected implicit branch. Prove the converse in the stated Dahlquist equivalence class.

**Proof route:** Complete the repeated-root proof; rewrite the recurrence as a companion system; prove uniformly bounded powers from the root condition; use variation of constants to propagate O(h^{p+1}) residuals over O(h^-1) steps. For necessity, use the consistency defect and unstable/parasitic homogeneous modes. Do not use one-step discrete Grönwall as a substitute for the root condition, and do not extend the equal-step proof to variable steps without new hypotheses.

**Examples:** zero-stable BDF2 with consistent starts; repeated interior root with bounded powers; repeated unit root with parasitic growth.

### NA-29 — Céa and Aubin–Nitsche error estimates

**Pages:** ceas-lemma-and-aubin-nitsche-error-estimates / ceas-lemma-and-aubin-nitsche-error-estimates-examples.

### NA-43 — Numerical optimization for statistical computation

**Pages:** numerical-optimization-for-statistical-computation / numerical-optimization-for-statistical-computation-examples.

**Scope:** For C² f on an open convex domain, an attained interior minimum and initial sublevel set compactly contained in that domain, require mI≼∇²f≼MI on a convex neighborhood containing that set and every trial segment used in the proof (alternatively impose the bounds globally). With m>0, prove exact-line-search gradient descent objective-gap contraction 1−m/M and the Armijo linear rate with 0<a<1/2, 0<b<1, initial trial step 1 and shrink factor b: accepted t≥min{1,2b(1−a)/M} yields gap contraction at most 1−2am min{1,2b(1−a)/M}. State objective gaps and iterate errors separately. For damped Newton require a Lipschitz Hessian on that convex trial neighborhood and prove finite damped steps followed by accepted unit steps and quadratic convergence. Prove ||x̃−x*||≤η/μ for a μ-strongly convex f when ||∇f(x̃)||≤η; include computed-gradient error δ by replacing η with η+δ. Do not assert global optimization for nonconvex or multimodal likelihoods.

**Proof route:** Use the descent lemma, strong convexity, Armijo decrease and Hessian-Lipschitz Taylor remainder under the stated sublevel invariance. For the gradient residual, use strong monotonicity and Cauchy–Schwarz. Separate optimization residual from an approximate objective/integral and from a model’s statistical target.

**Examples:** strongly convex quadratic with exact rate; damped Newton phase before quadratic convergence; small gradient at a poorly conditioned minimizer.

**Requires:** NA-09; published thm-hessian-characterises-convexity, thm-multivariable-taylor-formula-with-lagrange-remainder, and thm-gradient-and-hessian-of-the-frobenius-least-squares-functional where the least-squares objective is used.

**Sources:** Boyd–Vandenberghe, Convex Optimization §§9.2 and 9.3.1, physical PDF pp. 477–483 / printed pp. 463–469, and §§9.5.1–9.5.3, physical pp. 498–506 / printed pp. 484–492, proofs read: https://web.stanford.edu/~boyd/cvxbook/bv_cvxbook.pdf. These are convex-regime results only; statistics/sources.json source_id boyd-vandenberghe-convex-optimization-2004.

Define cyclic exact coordinate/block minimization, randomized coordinate gradient/proximal updates with independent uniform block sampling, separable nonsmooth g, per-block Lipschitz constants and finite inner solve tolerance. source_record_verbatim.scope:
genuinely-new periodic lattice-sum algorithm and error separation

A: `ewald-periodic-potentials-and-particle-mesh-error`.

On a specified 3D torus, finitely many distinct positions x_i and real charges q_i with sum q_i=0 define the mean-zero periodic Poisson distribution -Delta u=4pi(sum q_i delta_xi). Prove the Fourier distribution solution with zero mode fixed and the Gaussian Ewald decomposition of its off-source values/renormalized self energy. Specify the lattice shape, self subtraction, Gaussian parameter alpha, real/reciprocal cutoffs, output convention and arithmetic model. The naive Coulomb lattice sum is conditional; the periodic mean-zero definition controls the summation convention. Prove absolute convergence of the split sums, alpha independence, explicit Gaussian real-tail/reciprocal-tail bounds using lattice shell counts, and differentiated force bounds away from collisions. Include other boundary conventions only by separate explicit formula/proof.

For particle-mesh Ewald specify charge assignment degree/window, periodic grid, discrete Fourier solver, deconvolution restrictions, force differentiation and self correction. Prove error as real cutoff + reciprocal cutoff + assignment/aliasing + mesh differentiation + arithmetic, with actual window Fourier-decay/smoothness assumptions; O(N log N) FFT work alone is not an accuracy theorem. Point-source potentials are singular: any uniform field error is on a collision-free evaluation set, or is stated for a regularized source norm. N-body time integration, thermodynamic limits and singular mean-field limits remain separate.

Same-frontier PC-EWALD suppliers: Gaussian Poisson summation (reuse canonical Poisson theorem if its hypotheses fit), torus distribution Green function and zero mode, lattice shell Gaussian estimates, self limit, assignment Fourier aliases and force derivative bounds. Linear owner FFT; PDE owner periodic Poisson if it supplies the exact torus distribution interface; biology owner PIC consumes only the solver guarantee under matching regularization. B: neutral dipole cell, nonneutral zero-mode obstruction, alpha tradeoff at fixed tolerance, source collision, energy/force consistency. Sources: Ewald 1921 https://doi.org/10.1002/andp.19213690304 ; Darden–York–Pedersen PME https://doi.org/10.1063/1.464397 ; Essmann et al smooth PME https://doi.org/10.1063/1.470117 . Reading pending.

source_record_verbatim.title: High-resolution TVD, ENO and WENO reconstruction
source_record_verbatim.scope: Define MUSCL finite-volume reconstruction, a concrete minmod limiter, ENO stencil selection, WENO5-JS weights and a documented improved critical-point variant; distinguish finite-volume cell-average reconstruction from nodal finite differences. Prove second-order smooth-region reconstruction where the limiter is inactive; prove scalar TVD for a stated flux/limiter/CFL update by Harten's incremental form. Prove WENO polynomial reproduction/consistency and optimal smooth-region order under explicit smoothness and weight asymptotics; near critical points state the actual JS order, not automatic fifth order. Include the scalar linear monotonicity/order barrier. Systems characteristic reconstruction is defined but receives no automatic scalar TVD theorem.
source_record_verbatim.proof_route: Solve reconstruction moment equations; Taylor-expand candidate polynomials and smoothness indicators with uniform remainders; derive nonlinear weight asymptotics including epsilon scaling. Derive nonnegative incremental coefficients and sum their variation estimate. Give a concrete critical-point counterexample when hypotheses fail.
source_record_verbatim.examples: smooth advection, extrema clipping, Burgers shock, WENO critical point, oscillatory unlimited reconstruction.

source_record_verbatim.promise_and_proof_design_verbatim: **A scope.** Retarded y'=f(t,y(t),y(t-tau)), constant tau>0, Lipschitz f and continuous initial history on [-tau,0]. Method of steps gives existence/uniqueness; explicit Euler plus piecewise-linear stored-history interpolation gives order1 for Lipschitz exact trajectory with bounded piecewise derivatives, uniform step; disclose derivative jumps at k tau and align/restart if higher order. Distributed delays use a specified quadrature with separately bounded history error. Add scalar neutral y'(t)-a y'(t-tau)=f(t,y,y_delay), |a|<1, compatible C1 history and commensurate h=tau/m: prove bounded inverse of neutral difference I-a shift by geometric series and resulting first-order derivative/solution error under piecewise C2 regularity. ### T10/T11 hard-sphere addendum

For finitely many spherical particles with masses m_i>0, radii r_i>0 and smooth external forces on a compact separated configuration tube, define pair guard ||q_i-q_j||-(r_i+r_j). An isolated binary impact has unit normal n=(q_i-q_j)/||q_i-q_j|| and preimpact relative normal velocity v_n=(v_i-v_j) dot n<0. For prescribed restitution e in [0,1], impulse J=-(1+e)v_n/(1/m_i+1/m_j) gives v_i^+=v_i^-+J n/m_i, v_j^+=v_j^--J n/m_j. Prove total linear momentum conservation, normal relative velocity -e v_n and kinetic energy change -(1-e²)v_n²/[2(1/m_i+1/m_j)]. Tangential velocities are unchanged in this frictionless model. These are conditional mathematical collision laws, not a claim that restitution is constant in real materials. Event-driven integration invokes T10 transversality, dense trajectory/guard certificates, event separation, finite event count and restart residual error. Include collision search cost O(P²) naive and any spatial neighbor structure's actual assumptions. Simultaneous collisions, grazing v_n=0, dense frictional multi-contact and inelastic collapse/Zeno violate the isolated binary theorem; return explicit unresolved-event/budget status, or invoke a separately specified complementarity model. T11's scalar complementarity result is not advertised as uniqueness of arbitrary granular frictional contact. A DEM soft-contact penalty is a different ODE model; convergence of penalty to rigid impacts requires its own stiffness/restitution calibration limit and is not inferred from timestep convergence.

**Exact scope.** Use column probability vectors: finite Q has Q_ij≥0 for i≠j, 1ᵀQ=0. For ν≥max_j(−Q_jj)>0, P=I+Q/ν is column stochastic and

`p(t)=exp(tQ)p0 = Σ_{k≥0} exp(−νt)(νt)^k/k! P^k p0`.

Define finite Poisson-series accumulation with a certified tail bound and a maximum term budget; ν=0 returns p0. Prove nonnegative substochastic partial sums, l1 omitted probability exactly the scalar Poisson tail for normalized p0, and l1 total transient error ≤tail + accumulated arithmetic/algebraic error. A floating-point subtraction `1−sum` is not automatically a certified tail; use controlled interval sums or a proved geometric/Chernoff tail bound. Large νt must use time splitting or stable Poisson recurrences rather than silently underflowing `exp(−νt)`.

Finite-state projection: for an increasing finite set F in a countable nonexplosive chain, kill the process on first exit, or append an absorbing cemetery state carrying escaped mass. The killed state probability is componentwise ≤the full marginal restricted to F. Under a common-process coupling, l1 error after embedding the killed vector in the full state space equals lost mass; the absorbing projection including the cemetery state instead gives an observable error bound for bounded observables, with oscillation factor stated. Returning trajectories are a reason killed and restricted full probabilities differ. Adaptive enlargement requires a finite budget and certificates from each actual projection; existence of a finite set meeting a tolerance is separate.

`p(t)=exp(tQ)p0 = Σ_{k≥0} exp(−νt)(νt)^k/k! P^k p0`.

Define finite Poisson-series accumulation with a certified tail bound and a maximum term budget; ν=0 returns p0. Prove nonnegative substochastic partial sums, l1 omitted probability exactly the scalar Poisson tail for normalized p0, and l1 total transient error ≤tail + accumulated arithmetic/algebraic error. A floating-point subtraction `1−sum` is not automatically a certified tail; use controlled interval sums or a proved geometric/Chernoff tail bound. Large νt must use time splitting or stable Poisson recurrences rather than silently underflowing `exp(−νt)`.

Finite-state projection: for an increasing finite set F in a countable nonexplosive chain, kill the process on first exit, or append an absorbing cemetery state carrying escaped mass. The killed state probability is componentwise ≤the full marginal restricted to F. Under a common-process coupling, l1 error after embedding the killed vector in the full state space equals lost mass; the absorbing projection including the cemetery state instead gives an observable error bound for bounded observables, with oscillation factor stated. Returning trajectories are a reason killed and restricted full probabilities differ. With E_m=span{e₁,…,e_m}, define δ_h=sup_{v∈E_m, ||v||_a=1} inf_{w_h∈V_h}||v−w_h||_a, prove injectivity of the trial projection for sufficiently small δ_h, and bound λ_{h,m}−λ_m≤C_m δ_h². A coercive shift is removed from eigenvalues after the argument, preserving the ordering. For multiple eigenvalues compare invariant subspaces/gaps rather than arbitrary eigenvectors. A nonsymmetric/nonconforming Babuška–Osborn extension needs operator-norm convergence, uniform discrete stability, primal/adjoint approximation and generalized-eigenspace multiplicity hypotheses.

**Proof route:** Use the published continuous compact-resolvent spectral theorem and min–max. Apply the Galerkin min–max principle to the discrete form, then bound Rayleigh quotients by best approximation; derive eigenspace rates separately. For the nonsymmetric extension prove the compact-operator perturbation result before citing it.

**Examples:** conforming eigenvalue upper bound for Dirichlet Laplacian; repeated eigenvalue with converging eigenspace but unstable eigenvector choice; a nonconforming eigenvalue below the exact one.

**Requires:** NA-28 and NA-29; published thm-symmetric-elliptic-form-operator-is-self-adjoint-with-compact-resolvent, thm-discrete-spectrum-of-a-symmetric-elliptic-dirichlet-operator, thm-courant-fischer-minimax-for-elliptic-eigenvalues, and thm-spectral-theorem-for-compact-self-adjoint-operators.

**Sources:** Guermond Fall 2025 Chs. 46–48, complete stated PDFs, https://people.tamu.edu/~guermond/M661_FALL_2025/. The local source gives full symmetric conforming theory and additional nonnormal claims with stronger operator hypotheses; exact reviewed ranges are in fem-spectral/sources.json.

A: `periodic-orbit-shooting-collocation-and-floquet-error`.

Define shooting unknown (x0,T) with residual phi_T(x0)-x0 plus phase condition; multiple shooting and periodic collocation use time-owner algorithms. An autonomous periodic orbit has unit Floquet multiplier; impose phase transversality and simplicity of this unit multiplier so the augmented Newton derivative is invertible. Prove augmented-Jacobian characterization; residual-to-orbit local error and discretization error with explicit inverse/time sensitivity constants. Define monodromy by the variational IVP; compute Floquet multipliers with canonical Schur/eigensolver. Prove perturbation enclosure for separated simple multipliers (canonical left/right conditioning), cluster enclosures where necessary, and certification of orbital stability only when all nontrivial multiplier enclosures lie strictly inside the unit disk. No stability conclusion from finite precision values touching it.

Suppliers PC-PER: periodic phase quotient and bordered inverse; time owner flow/variational error; linear owner matrix/eigensolver perturbation; PC-BIF local existence if consumed. Sources: Doedel et al AUTO documentation https://indy.cs.concordia.ca/auto/ ; Kuznetsov above. Reading pending; software manual is an algorithm specification, not proof replacement.

source_record_verbatim.title: Positivity, invariant domains and entropy-stable systems fluxes
source_record_verbatim.scope: Define convex invariant sets and convex entropy pairs for systems. Prove a first-order local Lax–Friedrichs/HLL invariant-domain update under a stated invariant Riemann-average hypothesis and CFL convex-combination coefficients; prove ideal-gas density/internal-energy positivity on the explicitly admitted wave-speed branch. Define entropy variables, two-point entropy-conservative flux and dissipative entropy-stable flux. Prove the semidiscrete cell entropy inequality from the exact Tadmor jump condition and positive semidefinite dissipation. Fully discrete entropy needs its own time-step theorem. Define a convex scaling positivity limiter and prove cell-average conservation plus positive quadrature-node states; do not claim cellwise pointwise positivity from finitely many nodes without a separate argument.
source_record_verbatim.proof_route: Convexity of admissible Euler set; decompose updates into invariant Riemann averages. Multiply flux balances by entropy variables, telescope entropy potentials and bound dissipation. Limiter takes the maximal admissible scaling toward a positive mean; prove preservation and smooth-data accuracy only with a strict positive margin.
source_record_verbatim.examples: near-vacuum Euler, entropy residual, conservative positivity rescaling, entropy-stable but insufficiently resolved shock.

source_record_verbatim.title: Mixed H(div) fluxes, Darcy flow and local conservation
source_record_verbatim.scope: Define H(div), weak normal trace by Green duality, RT0/BDM spaces, contravariant Piola map, divergence-commuting interpolation on its proper regularity domain, and a stable RT0/P0 mixed Darcy method. Prove mixed well-posedness and flux/pressure error, exact element mass balance and normal-flux continuity. Define hybridization/static condensation and prove equivalence modulo pressure gauge. Coefficient-robust claims explicitly track permeability contrast and weighted norms.
source_record_verbatim.proof_route: Prove Lipschitz-cell normal trace boundedness using an H1 lifting and Green independence; construct RT unisolvence and divergence commuting from face moments. Construct a bounded commuting projection using smoothing when canonical moments are not defined on all H(div); prove discrete inf-sup from divergence lifting plus interpolation. Apply NA34 abstract mixed theorem; hybridization follows local elimination and face multiplier equations.

source_record_verbatim.promise_and_proof_design_verbatim:
**A scope.** Backward Euler, BDF2 implementation and a selected two-stage L-stable SDIRK (gamma=1-1/sqrt(2)); also Radau IIA as an explicit tableau/interface with concrete two-stage order3 and L-stability proved before advertised. Nonlinear stage residual equations, Newton/chord iteration and factorization reuse, consistent starts. Under f smooth/global Lipschitz on a common tube, hL small proves stage branch by contraction and order by Taylor; for dissipative f with <f(x)-f(y),x-y> <= -mu||x-y||² prove BE resolvent Lipschitz 1/(1+hmu), branch existence separately by strong monotonicity/coercivity (same-frontier prerequisite). Residual solve error rho_n contributes <= sum propagated ||rho_n||/(1+hmu). Do not impose hL small as the only stiff existence proof. Scalar RK stability follows from actual tableau rational function and half-plane algebra; no generic nonlinear L-stability conclusion.

**Proof route/prereqs.** Same-pair lemmas: finite-dimensional strongly monotone continuous onto map via coercivity/Brouwer (or minimization only for gradient f); contraction branch; SDIRK Taylor order2; two-stage Radau quadrature/stage order3 and rational-function A/L stability. Consume NA linear solves/Newton and current LMM theory. Explicit residual scaling distinguishes derivative residual from update residual. **B:** Robertson reaction equations (algorithm and measured work, no global analytical rate without bounded derivatives), stiff scalar decay with trapezoid ringing, nonlinear dissipative solve, Newton budget failure. **Cost:** Jacobian/factorization per refresh plus triangular solves per stage/Newton iteration; sparse complexity delegated actual matrix structure. **Sources:** Hairer/Wanner, Solving ODE II, Ch IV one-step stiff methods, BDF and implementation chapters; Butcher, Numerical Methods for ODEs, implicit RK/Radau. Full reads pending.

### NA-07 — Multigrid methods and complexity

**Pages:** multigrid-methods-and-complexity / multigrid-methods-and-complexity-examples.

**Scope:** Define fine/coarse spaces, prolongation P, restriction R, Galerkin operator A_H=RA_hP, smoothing step, two-grid error operator, and one stated V-cycle. Prove the Galerkin coarse correction is an A_h-orthogonal projector for SPD A_h under the stated transfer identities. Prove the two-grid contraction from smoothing and approximation inequalities with constants 0<α≤β uniform in mesh level; keep convergence separate from cycle work. State the recursion T(N)=cN+γT(N/2^d) with its three Master-theorem regimes. FMG order and AMG selection are separate conditional claims; no arbitrary algebraic coarsening is declared convergent.

**Proof route:** Derive the projector identity, then use the exact smoothing and approximation estimates to obtain the one-sided bound sqrt(1−α/β); for symmetric pre/post smoothing use the A_h-adjoint relation. Prove work by recursion-tree counting. A mesh-independent rate requires level-uniform α,β; a rediscretized operator is not identified with the Galerkin operator without an equality proof.

**Examples:** 1D Poisson with linear interpolation; one coarse correction on a smooth error; V-cycle and W-cycle costs under γ=1 and γ=2 in d=2.

**Requires:** NA-03 and NA-06; published Linear Algebra matrix norm and SPD suppliers. For PDE model examples also use published PDE page lax-milgram-and-weak-elliptic-solutions.

**Sources:** Saad Ch. 13 §§13.1–13.7, printed pp. 423–468, read in full, including Lemma 13.1, Theorems 13.2–13.3 and their proof routes: https://www-users.cse.umn.edu/~saad/IterMethBook_2ndEd.pdf; Cornell notes 32–33, complete PDFs, https://www.cs.cornell.edu/~bindel/class/cs6210-f12/lectures.html. Source proof limits and the heuristic scope of AMG are in iterative/sources.json.

source_record_verbatim.promise_and_proof_design_verbatim:
Genuinely-new global numerical optimization, separate from finding nonconvex stationary points. On a compact box, define spatial branch-and-bound with a finite budget, a rigorous lower-bounding oracle, feasible incumbents, deterministic splitting and epsilon gap termination. Prove global epsilon-optimality from the invariant lower≤inf over each live box and incumbent feasibility; prove eventual epsilon termination when bounds are consistent as box diameter→0, subdivisions are exhaustive and the objective is continuous. Instantiate interval/Lipschitz bounds using the linear/approximation agent's validated arithmetic contracts and locally proved convex McCormick envelopes for products; relaxations must enclose the objective/constraints including floating-point error. For constrained problems, pruning requires a proved infeasibility bound; empty feasible set detection needs a separate separation margin, not mere continuity. Define mixed-integer branch-and-bound for bounded integer domains with certified continuous relaxation bounds, finite enumeration fallback and exact gap certificate; do not claim polynomial complexity. Include derivative-free Bayesian optimization as a separate finite acquisition procedure consuming published GP posterior laws, with no generic global theorem unless an explicit RKHS/GP confidence-and-information-gain contract is proved locally; acquisition maximization error is retained. Sources: Horst–Tuy, *Global Optimization*, branch-and-bound chapters; Moore–Kearfott–Cloud, *Introduction to Interval Analysis*, global optimization chapter; McCormick (1976), factorable nonconvex relaxation; Srinivas et al. (2010), GP-UCB regret theorem with exact kernel/noise assumptions selected at authoring. B: multimodal polynomial certified gap, engineering mixed design, invalid lower bound loses optimum, noisy biological simulator Bayesian search whose surrogate uncertainty is conditional on the kernel/model. Dependencies OPT5/7 relaxations, NA01/09, validated arithmetic owner, existing BCS GP posterior; owner supplies bounding/exhaustiveness/relaxation and any GP-UCB concentration/information-gain prerequisites in this same frontier. No validated root-solving algorithm is duplicated.

### OPT12: `global-optimization-and-certified-branch-and-bound`

Genuinely-new global numerical optimization, separate from finding nonconvex stationary points. On a compact box, define spatial branch-and-bound with a finite budget, a rigorous lower-bounding oracle, feasible incumbents, deterministic splitting and epsilon gap termination. Prove global epsilon-optimality from the invariant lower≤inf over each live box and incumbent feasibility; prove eventual epsilon termination when bounds are consistent as box diameter→0, subdivisions are exhaustive and the objective is continuous. Instantiate interval/Lipschitz bounds using the linear/approximation agent's validated arithmetic contracts and locally proved convex McCormick envelopes for products; relaxations must enclose the objective/constraints including floating-point error. For constrained problems, pruning requires a proved infeasibility bound; empty feasible set detection needs a separate separation margin, not mere continuity. Define mixed-integer branch-and-bound for bounded integer domains with certified continuous relaxation bounds, finite enumeration fallback and exact gap certificate; do not claim polynomial complexity. Include derivative-free Bayesian optimization as a separate finite acquisition procedure consuming published GP posterior laws, with no generic global theorem unless an explicit RKHS/GP confidence-and-information-gain contract is proved locally; acquisition maximization error is retained. source_record_verbatim.title: Nonlinear parabolic compactness and monotone evolution
source_record_verbatim.scope: Prove the Aubin–Lions compactness contract for V compactly embedded H continuously embedded V*, with Lp-in-time V bounds (1<p<infinity) and a positive-exponent V* time-derivative/translate bound; state exactly the strong intermediate-space/time exponent obtained, and its precise piecewise-constant discrete time-translate analogue. Define coercive monotone diffusion with growth matched to p-Laplacian energy (for the H=L2 branch require p>max(1,2d/(d+2)) so W1p embeds compactly in L2) and backward Euler/FEM approximation; prove discrete existence, energy bounds and subsequential convergence/identification by Minty's argument under stated reflexivity and monotonicity. Strong monotonicity/Lipschitz or smooth-solution assumptions give separate quantitative errors; no unconditional smooth rate for degenerate porous-medium fronts.
source_record_verbatim.proof_route: Finite-rank compact approximation of V unit ball in H, time translates from the V* derivative, finite-dimensional time compactness and interpolation yield strong L2 compactness; provide endpoint exponents and reconstruction defects. Browder–Minty construction is local if absent: finite Galerkin/Brouwer, weak compactness, monotone graph identification and uniqueness. Apply discrete integration by parts, weak lower semicontinuity and Minty limsup criterion to nonlinear flux.
source_record_verbatim.examples: p-Laplacian, porous-medium finite propagation, failure of linear Ritz commutation, time oscillations without derivative control.

source_record_verbatim.promise_and_proof_design_verbatim: **A scope.** A specific tamed Euler scheme b_h=b/(1+h|b|) for autonomous globally one-sided Lipschitz polynomial-growth drift and globally Lipschitz diffusion, all required initial moments. Prove strong order1/2 with moment control; state exact differentiability/polynomial derivative assumptions needed for chosen theorem. Also drift-implicit backward Euler for monotone dissipative drift with a uniquely solvable implicit resolvent and Lipschitz diffusion, mean-square stability and finite-time rate under stated regularity. CIR dX=k(theta-X)dt+sigma sqrt(X)dW, X0>0, k,theta,sigma>0 and 2k theta>=sigma²: define Z=sqrt(X), a=(4k theta-sigma²)/8>0, and take the positive root of (1+k h/2) Znew²-(Z+sigma DeltaW/2)Znew-a h=0. Prove strict numerical positivity directly; prove strong convergence in probability on finite horizons by stopped locally Lipschitz Lamperti analysis and a same-pair nonattainment/exit-probability theorem. Do not promise an Lp rate absent inverse-moment assumptions. This is a concrete implicit square-root algorithm, not ordinary EM. **Proof:** same-pair Lyapunov moment/localization and monotone SDE existence extension beyond global Lipschitz; tamed moment domination and defect recurrence with stopping removal, resolvent inequality for implicit scheme. A source theorem's long proof is an authoring obligation, not a missing external supplier. **B:** cubic dissipative drift where EM moments diverge; positive CIR boundary; noise-induced stability. **Deps:** published Itô/isometry, T01, T13 local-to-global where compatible; own all non-global-Lipschitz model existence/moments. **Cost:** drift taming vs nonlinear solve, rejected branch/failure explicitly. **Sources:** Hutzenthaler/Jentzen/Kloeden, Proc Royal Society A 467 (2011), explicit divergence; Ann Appl Probab 22 (2012), strong convergence of tamed methods; Higham/Mao/Stuart, SIAM J Numer Anal 40 (2002); Alfonsi CIR schemes (chosen full theorem must be read). **Proof:** consistency induction proves U_n^k=F^n(u0) for n<=k, hence exact fine solution after at most N sweeps in exact arithmetic, independent of a contraction assertion. The resulting matrix has nonpositive off-diagonals, positive diagonal and strict column dominance; prove inverse nonnegativity, positivity and exact summed conservation. The specified second-order positive-interior scheme is MPRK22(1): compute the stage z by Patankar Euler with denominator y^n; then solve `y_i^{n+1}=y_i^n+Δt Σ_j[(p_ij(y^n)+p_ij(z)) y_j^{n+1}/(2z_j)−(d_ij(y^n)+d_ij(z)) y_i^{n+1}/(2z_i)]`. **Exact scope.** Start from a stipulated linear renewal transport problem `n_t+n_a=−μ(a)n`, age a≥0, `n(t,0)=∫β(a)n(t,a)da`, nonnegative bounded Lipschitz μ,β and finite integrable initial density. Define finite-volume cell masses, explicit upwind transport/loss, positive quadrature for births, finite age cutoff and specified outflow. Prove nonnegative update under transport-plus-loss CFL; l1 growth `||n_h^{k+1}||1≤(1+Δt||β||∞)||n_h^k||1`; obtain stability for the difference of two data sets. Prove first-order mesh/time/quadrature convergence under explicit smoothness, compatible initial renewal boundary and bounded finite horizon. If compatibility is absent, prove an L1/BV route with reduced regularity rather than reusing the smooth Taylor theorem. State separate age-tail and survival/outflow bounds; finite maximum age is a truncation of an infinite-age model.

Extend to size transport `∂_t n+∂_x(g(x)n)=−μn` with g≥g_min>0 and a specified nonlocal birth/division kernel. Use flux variables and positive quadrature, deriving the changed CFL/weighted mass identities. Include cohort/characteristic quadrature as a distinct procedure with consistency proof; zero growth, discontinuous coefficients and moving size boundaries need their own hypotheses. A delay equation is not automatically equivalent without a proved renewal/characteristic identity.

preserved_original_design.approved_section_verbatim:
### NA-13 — Gaussian quadrature

**Pages:** gaussian-quadrature / gaussian-quadrature-examples.

**Scope:** For positive dμ=w(x)dx on [a,b], finite moments through degree 2m for the remainder integral (degree 2m−1 suffices for rule exactness), and a positive-definite polynomial inner product through degree m for the remainder branch, construct the monic orthogonal polynomial p_m. Prove it has m simple roots in (a,b); the m-node Gauss rule at those roots has positive weights and exactness through degree 2m−1. For f∈C^{2m}[a,b], prove the remainder f^{(2m)}(ξ)/(2m)! ∫p_m²dμ. Tensor products preserve coordinatewise exactness but cost exponentially in dimension.

**Proof route:** Use Gram–Schmidt; prove root count by sign changes; divide q=p_mr+s and use orthogonality for exactness; apply exactness to ℓ_i² for positive weights; use Hermite interpolation at double nodes and repeated Rolle for the remainder. Each intermediate theorem is an explicit local proof obligation. To retain the exactness-only degree-2m−1 moment variant, construct p_m from its m orthogonality equations using the degree-(m−1) positive moment matrix and nonzero density support; do not pretend a degree-m quadratic norm is defined without the degree-2m moment.

**Examples:** two-node Gauss–Legendre exact through degree three; positive weights from ℓ_i²; a tensor-product node-count calculation.

**Requires:** NA-10 and published Linear Algebra page inner-product-spaces-and-orthogonality.

**Sources:** Owen, Ch. 7, complete extracted chapter read, https://artowen.su.domains/mc/Ch-quadrature.pdf. It states Gaussian exactness and error but points to outside proofs; no proof is imported from that chapter. See statistics/sources.json source_id owen-monte-carlo-book-2009-2023-selected-chapters.

source_record_verbatim.title: Evolutionary incompressible flow discretization
source_record_verbatim.scope: Define weak incompressible Navier–Stokes on bounded Lipschitz domains in d=2,3 with viscosity nu>0, homogeneous Dirichlet data and pressure gauge. Use NA34's actual stable mini-element pair and a skew-symmetric convective form. Reuse existing finite-dimensional Brouwer; prove existence of a backward-Euler finite-dimensional discrete solution, discrete energy inequality and subsequential convergence to a weak solution for a specified mesh/time family; uniqueness is conditional in 3D. Prove a velocity/pressure error bound only on a supplied sufficiently smooth exact solution interval, with explicit norms and nu-dependent constants. Do not assert Reynolds-uniform robustness from an ordinary Gronwall estimate.
source_record_verbatim.proof_route: Brouwer fixed-point existence using the discrete energy outward-pointing bound and existing `thm-brouwer-fixed-point-theorem` (prove only the outward-pointing-zero corollary); derive skew cancellation, pressure cancellation and energy. Prove discrete Sobolev and trilinear bounds by NA28 scaling/root Sobolev. Use PE12 time-translate compactness for strong L2 velocity and pass convection; derive divergence/initial trace and weak energy lower semicontinuity. Smooth errors use approximation, discrete inf-sup and Gronwall.
source_record_verbatim.examples: 2D Taylor–Green manufactured flow, energy budget, pressure gauge, unresolved 3D turbulence as a conditional computation.

source_record_verbatim.title: Overlapping Schwarz and stable subspace decompositions
source_record_verbatim.scope: Define local restriction/prolongation, additive and multiplicative Schwarz, exact/inexact local solves and a coarse space for SPD conforming diffusion. Prove the abstract additive Schwarz condition bound from a stable decomposition constant C0 and a strengthened Cauchy–Schwarz/overlap constant C1; give the precise norm and normalization so the bound is C0*C1. Prove multiplicative contraction from the associated subspace correction estimate with its actual constants. Then prove a two-level overlapping P1 Poisson specialization on quasiuniform shape-regular meshes, shape-regular subdomains, coarse diameter H and overlap delta, with explicit H/delta dependence and bounded overlap. A one-level method does not receive a uniform-in-subdomain-count bound. High coefficient contrast and anisotropy require separately constructed robust coarse spaces; the ordinary partition proof does not imply robustness.
source_record_verbatim.proof_route: Local energy minimization expresses B inverse as the minimum summed local energy over decompositions. Lower/upper Rayleigh bounds follow from stable decomposition and bounded synthesis, using existing SPD/CG suppliers. Construct a boundary-preserving coarse quasi-interpolant (NA28 lower-regularity interface) and partition-of-unity theta_i with ||grad theta_i||≤C/delta; decompose u into coarse part plus interpolated theta_i(u-u0), then prove local interpolation/overlap bounds and stable energy estimates. Multiplicative correction uses exact projection error products, telescoped energy decreases and a proved stable-decomposition estimate; noncommuting projections cannot simply multiply scalar contraction factors. Inexact local solvers require uniform spectral equivalence and resulting modified constants.

pairs.title: Overlapping Schwarz and stable subspace decompositions
pairs.scope: Define local restriction/prolongation, additive and multiplicative Schwarz, exact/inexact local solves and a coarse space for SPD conforming diffusion. Prove the abstract additive Schwarz condition bound from a stable decomposition constant C0 and a strengthened Cauchy–Schwarz/overlap constant C1; give the precise norm and normalization so the bound is C0*C1. Prove multiplicative contraction from the associated subspace correction estimate with its actual constants. Then prove a two-level overlapping P1 Poisson specialization on quasiuniform shape-regular meshes, shape-regular subdomains, coarse diameter H and overlap delta, with explicit H/delta dependence and bounded overlap. A one-level method does not receive a uniform-in-subdomain-count bound. High coefficient contrast and anisotropy require separately constructed robust coarse spaces; the ordinary partition proof does not imply robustness.
pairs.proof_routes: Local energy minimization expresses B inverse as the minimum summed local energy over decompositions. Lower/upper Rayleigh bounds follow from stable decomposition and bounded synthesis, using existing SPD/CG suppliers. Construct a boundary-preserving coarse quasi-interpolant (NA28 lower-regularity interface) and partition-of-unity theta_i with ||grad theta_i||≤C/delta; decompose u into coarse part plus interpolated theta_i(u-u0), then prove local interpolation/overlap bounds and stable energy estimates. Multiplicative correction uses exact projection error products, telescoped energy decreases and a proved stable-decomposition estimate; noncommuting projections cannot simply multiply scalar contraction factors. Inexact local solvers require uniform spectral equivalence and resulting modified constants.

source_record_verbatim.title: Nonlinear full-approximation multigrid
source_record_verbatim.scope: Define FAS for F_h(u_h)=f_h with iterate restriction I_h^H, residual restriction R_h^H, prolongation P_H^h, coarse operator F_H and tau correction; specify nonlinear pre/post smoothing and finite budgets/branch failure. Prove fine-root fixed-point consistency for arbitrary consistent transfers when the coarse right side is F_H(Iu)+R(f-F_h(u)); require the coarse solver return the selected root Iu at zero defect. Prove exact reduction to linear correction multigrid when operators/smoothers/coarse solves are linear. Prove local convergence near a root from a bound q<1 on the derivative of the actual FAS cycle plus a proved Lipschitz derivative bound and invariant radius. Give a semilinear monotone diffusion example with actually verified smooth branch/smoother/coarse assumptions. Mesh-independent basin/rate requires those constants uniformly in h; no arbitrary nonlinear FAS convergence claim.
source_record_verbatim.proof_route: Substitute the exact root and telescope the coarse correction. Differentiate every smoother, restriction, implicit coarse branch and prolongation at the root; use the local implicit theorem for the coarse Jacobian inverse and derive the linearized two-grid error operator exactly. NA07 contraction applies only when this derivative equals a linear cycle satisfying its actual smoothing/approximation hypotheses. Mean-value integral yields ||E(u)-u*||≤(q+Lr/2)||u-u*|| on the stated ball; choose r with q+Lr/2<1, prove invariance and iteration contraction. Coarse inexact solves add a quantified residual-to-correction defect with its own inverse bound. Cost recurrence includes nonlinear smoothing/coarse work, not a blanket O(N).
source_record_verbatim.examples: nonlinear reaction Poisson tau cancellation, zero-tau inconsistent fixed point, linear FAS equivalence, loss of local basin near a bifurcation.

**Exact scope.** Define finite discrete cluster aggregation/fragmentation by binary event rates and stoichiometric increments. Positive event rates and pair identities establish number/mass moments directly. Define conservative sectional/fixed-pivot redistribution on a finite positive mass grid: each product lying between adjacent pivots is split by nonnegative barycentric weights summing to one and reproducing its mass. Product above the cutoff enters a **reported lost-mass reservoir**, not an invented last-bin particle. In fragmentation, a reservoir does not preserve the true later return dynamics; either resolve the overflow state with its physical transition law or label it as truncation and bound omitted return error. Combine positivity CFL or XD-03 stepping with exact event mass accounting. Prove finite-dimensional convergence to the specified discrete/sectional ODE, with quadrature, temporal and cutoff contributions separated.

For a continuous-size theorem, require bounded Lipschitz aggregation and fragmentation kernels, declared fragment moment normalization, finite initial first/second moments and finite horizon. Own measure-valued well-posedness and bounded-Lipschitz stability, product-kernel quadrature error and first/second-moment propagation before deriving a grid consistency/stability bound. Weighted tail control is explicit, e.g. `∫_{x>R}x μ_t(dx)≤R^−1∫x² μ_t(dx)`, with the actual second-moment differential bound. An unbounded superlinear coagulation kernel may gel; no mass-conserving global theorem is inferred from finite-grid conservation. Include a counterexample demonstrating this limitation rather than narrowing the mathematical model silently.

Product above the cutoff enters a **reported lost-mass reservoir**, not an invented last-bin particle. In fragmentation, a reservoir does not preserve the true later return dynamics; either resolve the overflow state with its physical transition law or label it as truncation and bound omitted return error. Combine positivity CFL or XD-03 stepping with exact event mass accounting. Prove finite-dimensional convergence to the specified discrete/sectional ODE, with quadrature, temporal and cutoff contributions separated.

For a continuous-size theorem, require bounded Lipschitz aggregation and fragmentation kernels, declared fragment moment normalization, finite initial first/second moments and finite horizon. Own measure-valued well-posedness and bounded-Lipschitz stability, product-kernel quadrature error and first/second-moment propagation before deriving a grid consistency/stability bound. Weighted tail control is explicit, e.g. `∫_{x>R}x μ_t(dx)≤R^−1∫x² μ_t(dx)`, with the actual second-moment differential bound. **Exact scope.** Symmetric normalized compactly supported kernel W_ε and cell/particle quadrature with fill distance and bounded cell volumes. The specified SPH system has `ρ_i=Σ_j m_j W_ε(x_i−x_j)`, `x_i′=v_i`, and `v_i′=−Σ_j m_j(p_i/ρ_i²+p_j/ρ_j²)∇W_ε(x_i−x_j)`, positive masses, a C² radial kernel and a proved lower bound on ρ_i on the controlled tube. The equations are (I-K)u=f and (I-K_n)u_n=f_n. In the operator-norm route prove ||K-K_n||<=epsilon_n in the stated X/operator spaces; if ||(I-K)^-1|| epsilon_n<1, derive discrete inverse bound and ||u-u_n|| <= ||(I-K_n)^-1|| (||f-f_n||+||(K-K_n)u||). **Do not assert norm convergence on C for arbitrary point-sampling quadrature**: standard Nyström commonly needs the collectively compact route. Prove pointwise consistency and collective compactness (uniform boundedness/equicontinuity), then uniform discrete invertibility from contradiction/compact subsequences and continuous injectivity. Error rate uses quadrature of k(x,.)u(.), with its actual regularity, not all continuous unit-ball functions. Include a singular-kernel product-integration instance with weight stability and consistency proved, not assumed.
