genuinely-new transition-state and minimum-energy-path numerics

A: `minimum-energy-paths-string-neb-and-saddle-certificates`.

For a supplied C^4 finite-dimensional potential V on a declared collision-free tube, define a regular minimum-energy path by (I-t t^T)grad V=0 and prescribed endpoint conditions; the physical relevance of V is outside this conditional mathematics. Define a finite-image string method (gradient update plus specified arc-length redistribution/interpolation) and NEB with explicit tangent selection, spring force, endpoint treatment, ties/degenerate segment failure, finite budgets and stop criteria. Climbing-image changes the residual and needs its own exact formula. A small NEB force is not automatically a small continuum path error.

Prove central-difference unit-tangent approximation O(h²) for C^3 arc-length paths with nonvanishing derivative and quasiuniform, appropriately symmetric sampling; nonuniform formulas must use actual unequal-step coefficients. Derive discrete projected-force consistency O(h²) away from tangent degeneracy, plus the chosen spring/reparametrization residual on sampled arc-length paths. If the phase/parameterization-fixed discrete residual Jacobians have a **proved or independently certified uniform inverse bound** and a matching Lipschitz neighborhood, apply existing quantitative Newton/IFT to obtain a nearby discrete path and residual-to-path error; continuum convergence requires an actual stable interpolation/comparison theorem. PC-PATH owns that theorem for the stated stable smooth isolated path class, including endpoint and parameterization gauge. No blanket string/NEB convergence for every potential or mesh.

Define eigenvector-following with spectral ordering, one negative mode, eigensolve tolerance and branch failure; near a nondegenerate index-one critical point the exact selected local step equals the appropriate Newton critical-point solve, whose local quadratic guarantee is reused rather than reintroduced. Define a dimer Hessian-vector estimate using paired force evaluations; Taylor gives O(epsilon²) deterministic Hessian-vector bias under the stated derivatives, plus force error O(eta/epsilon). Prove separated-mode eigenvector error and its effect on a local inexact saddle iteration; mode tracking needs a gap. Certify Hessian index one through eigenvalue enclosures bounded away from zero, and retain finite residual/conditioning errors. This is a local mathematical saddle certificate, not proof of a molecular reaction rate or global transition mechanism.

Same-frontier suppliers PC-PATH: tangent/interpolation/reparametrization consistency; gauge-fixed stable path comparison theorem; local dimer/selected-mode perturbation and error propagation. Optimization owner OPT3 supplies generic nonconvex trust-region algebra, OPT11 manifold retraction if used; canonical `alg-damped-newton` / NA09 supply local root solving; linear spectral perturbation supplies separated-mode bounds. No generic optimizer is duplicated. B: curved double well, incorrect straight path, corner/cusp tangent failure, a saddle with wrong Morse index, near-degenerate two-mode dimer, finite-difference bias versus force noise tradeoff. Sources to inspect: Henkelman–Jónsson improved tangent NEB https://doi.org/10.1063/1.1323224 ; Henkelman–Uberuaga–Jónsson climbing image https://doi.org/10.1063/1.1329672 ; E–Ren–Vanden-Eijnden simplified string https://doi.org/10.1063/1.2720838 ; Henkelman–Jónsson dimer https://doi.org/10.1063/1.480097 . These are candidate algorithm sources, with full mathematical guarantee sources/proofs still an authoring obligation.

genuinely-new stable special-function algorithms

A: `stable-special-function-recurrences-and-certified-evaluation`.

Do not reauthor gamma/Bessel definitions. Reuse existing `def-euler-gamma-function`, `thm-stirling-formula-gamma`, `thm-gamma-functional-equation` only after exact statement inspection. Define finite-budget domain-partitioned evaluators for exp-scaled Bessel/modified Bessel and Airy, Fresnel sine/cosine integrals, gamma/log-gamma, erf/erfc, and a representative hypergeometric function. extend NA-37 and a substantial new nonlinear electronic-structure pair

A: `finite-basis-projector-energies-and-variational-electronic-structure`.

Let S be a supplied Hermitian positive-definite overlap matrix, 0 < r < n, and transform to an orthonormal basis using an existing Cholesky/spectral factorization. Define the compact set P_r = {P=P*, P²=P, tr P=r}. Input finite h=h*, a self-adjoint real-linear map G on Hermitian matrices, and optional real C² functional E_xc on a neighborhood of P_r. Define E(P)=tr(hP)+1/2 tr(PG(P))+E_xc(P) and its Hermitian Frobenius-gradient F(P)=h+G(P)+grad E_xc(P). The conditional finite-basis HF case is E_xc=0 with a supplied symmetry-compatible Coulomb/exchange tensor; the KS-like case is an explicitly supplied density map and differentiable chosen functional. These are mathematical definitions, not assertions of physical exactness. Prove a global minimizer exists, first variation along P(t)=e^{tK}Pe^{-tK} yields [F(P),P]=0, and a sufficient positive tangent-Hessian condition gives an isolated strict local minimizer modulo orbital gauge. A commutator-zero point need not be a minimum and need not occupy the lowest r eigenvalues. Do not silently equate stationarity and Aufbau SCF.

Also include the finite-temperature density domain 0<=D<=I, tr D=r with continuous endpoint convention 0 log 0=0 and entropy term beta^(-1) tr(D log D+(I-D)log(I-D)). Prove compact-domain minimizer existence; on the interior derive the Fermi–Dirac stationarity equation with chemical potential chosen for the trace, and prove uniqueness of that chemical potential for a fixed finite Hermitian F and 0<r<n. This does not prove uniqueness of a self-consistent density for a nonconvex energy. PC-VAR owns spectral trace derivative and endpoint-continuity suppliers; generic constrained KKT/prox comes from optimization owner.

For nested trial spaces, the finite-basis infimum decreases toward the infimum over their union; equality with a continuum infimum additionally requires density in the energy topology and continuity/liminf hypotheses, each proved for the chosen functional. No general Coulomb HF/DFT existence theorem is smuggled into this statement. Source-model error stays separate.

NA-37 amendment, no extra pair: for a normalized Ritz vector u with Rayleigh quotient mu and residual rho=||(A-mu)u||, prove dist(mu,spec A)<=rho. If a specific simple target eigenvalue is separated by certified gap delta from all others, prove sin(angle(u,e))<=rho/delta using spectral expansion; add an upper energy bound from min–max. A residual alone cannot identify the lowest eigenvalue. For a ground state on a compact-resolvent form domain carry the actual form/duality norm and continuum regularity, not the finite-matrix formula verbatim.

Proof route: bounded closed polynomial projector set is compact; Weierstrass; differentiate matrix traces and commutator curves; characterize all tangent directions as [K,P]; Taylor on local graph charts; spectral expansion for residuals; monotone infima plus explicit approximants for trial density. Same-frontier new suppliers owned PC-VAR: projector tangent/graph chart and gauge invariance, compactness, energy derivative/Hessian. Reuse canonical matrix differential, Courant–Fischer and optimization-owner retraction items.

B: two-level nonlinear projector with a stationary maximum; overlapping basis with ill-conditioned S; incomplete CI energy above its finite Hamiltonian ground energy; nested trial energies; nonsmooth chosen E_xc where the C² theorem fails.

Sources to inspect before authoring: Cancès–Le Bris, Can we outperform the DIIS approach for electronic structure calculations?, https://doi.org/10.1002/1097-461X(2000)79:2%3C82::AID-QUA3%3E3.0.CO;2-I . Citations here are candidate source locations, not completed reading evidence.

source_record_verbatim.title: Projection, pressure correction and saddle-point solvers
source_record_verbatim.scope: Define a concrete first-order incremental pressure-correction algorithm with explicit predictor, discrete projection, pressure update and boundary conditions; prove mass-inner-product projection and a matching energy estimate. Prove first-order velocity accuracy on the precise periodic smooth-data branch first; bounded-domain pressure and boundary-layer rates require separate hypotheses and proofs. Define rotational/second-order variants without claiming their rates until individually proved. Include block factorization and pressure Schur-complement preconditioners, proving spectral equivalence only from NA34 inf-sup/coercivity plus specified mass/stiffness scalings; this result supplies actual solver estimates, not generic improvement.
source_record_verbatim.proof_route: Orthogonal decomposition and pressure increment square identity; derive splitting error equation, retain artificial pressure boundary term, estimate in appropriate dual norms, then time Gronwall. Periodicity removes the boundary defect only in that theorem. Reuse `def-block-lu-factorisation` and `thm-block-lu-factorisation-via-an-invertible-leading-block`; derive only the PDE Schur energy identity and uniform spectral bounds; bound supremum quotient with inf-sup. No pressure Poisson solve silently imposes physical pressure data.

pairs.title: Projection, pressure correction and saddle-point solvers
pairs.scope: Define a concrete first-order incremental pressure-correction algorithm with explicit predictor, discrete projection, pressure update and boundary conditions; prove mass-inner-product projection and a matching energy estimate. Prove first-order velocity accuracy on the precise periodic smooth-data branch first; bounded-domain pressure and boundary-layer rates require separate hypotheses and proofs. Define rotational/second-order variants without claiming their rates until individually proved. Include block factorization and pressure Schur-complement preconditioners, proving spectral equivalence only from NA34 inf-sup/coercivity plus specified mass/stiffness scalings; this result supplies actual solver estimates, not generic improvement.
pairs.proof_routes: Orthogonal decomposition and pressure increment square identity; derive splitting error equation, retain artificial pressure boundary term, estimate in appropriate dual norms, then time Gronwall. Periodicity removes the boundary defect only in that theorem. Reuse `def-block-lu-factorisation` and `thm-block-lu-factorisation-via-an-invertible-leading-block`; derive only the PDE Schur energy identity and uniform spectral bounds; bound supremum quotient with inf-sup. No pressure Poisson solve silently imposes physical pressure data.

source_record_verbatim.title: Substructuring, FETI-DP and BDDC
source_record_verbatim.scope: Define discrete harmonic extension, interface Schur complement, primal assembled versus partially assembled interface spaces, primal constraints (corners/edge averages as appropriate), scaled averaging and a concrete BDDC method. Define corresponding FETI-DP dual multipliers/jump operator with explicit redundant-constraint convention. Prove well-definedness after removing local floating-subdomain nullspaces and establishing primal constraints; prove exact interface equivalence and the appropriate common nontrivial-spectrum comparison. Prove the classical bound C(1+log(H/h))² only for a stated scalar second-order diffusion family on shape-regular polygonal subdomains in 2D with matching quasiuniform triangulations and the selected corner/edge constraints/scaling; coefficient jumps need precisely stated subdomain-constant aligned coefficient/scaling assumptions. A 3D claim must add its edge/face constraint and trace proof. Do not claim arbitrary graph/mesh/high-contrast scalability.
source_record_verbatim.proof_route: Reuse block elimination for Schur algebra. Prove harmonic extension minimizes energy, then characterize the BDDC preconditioner by constrained local minimization and averaging. Prove averaging energy bound using the exact discrete trace/H1/2 norm and vertex-cutoff logarithmic estimate; this logarithmic estimate, local trace lifting and stable coarse constraint construction are same-page analytic prerequisites with full proofs, not assumed universal inequalities. Show dual jump/averaging decomposition identities and map eigenvectors between primal and dual operators, explicitly excluding null/unit modes where required. Work/storage counts are separate from conditioning and depend on local/coarse solver costs.
source_record_verbatim.examples: two floating Poisson subdomains, missing corner singularity, matching primal/dual spectrum, coarse-solve work bottleneck.

Assume semigroup bound ||exp(tA)||<=M exp(omega t), g C2 on controlled tube; fixed-A global order1/2, constants may depend on A. Define entire phi_k at zero. **Proof:** Duhamel identity then time Taylor/integral remainder, discrete convolution propagation; each approximate action error delta_n adds with the semigroup propagation bound. source_record_verbatim.promise_and_proof_design_verbatim:
**Disposition:** extend-existing numerical guarantee; consume NA15 RK/collocation and NA21 BVP collocation where actually established; this pair concerns IVP high-order quadrature and iterative solution, not duplicate BVP definitions.

On [t,t+h] with distinct nodes c_i in [0,1], let Q_ij=integral_0^ci l_j(s)ds from Lagrange basis. Collocation stage vector satisfies U=1 tensor u+h Q F(U). Explicitly define lower-triangular Q_delta from node-subinterval Euler quadrature; SDC sweep solves U^(k+1)=1 tensor u+h Q_delta F(U^(k+1))+h(Q-Q_delta)F(U^k), component by component with selected implicit branches or explicit preconditioner. If h L||Q_delta||<1, inverse Lipschitz inequality gives contraction factor q=h L||Q-Q_delta||/(1-h L||Q_delta||)<1. Prove stage fixed point equals collocation, geometric iteration residual bound, and finite budget reports nonconvergence. With sufficiently small h and constant predictor, each sweep reduces stage error by O(h); derive the actual order-vs-sweep index rather than promise unlimited order.

Prove local defect O(h^(M+1)) for M nodes from interpolation remainder assuming C^M smooth integrand along the exact flow, and stable propagation gives at least global order M for a step endpoint derived from the same quadrature. Gauss nodes endpoint superconvergence order2M is a separate full proof obligation using orthogonality/defect adjoint or exact RK order conditions; it cannot be inferred from polynomial degree alone. Include one fully proved Gauss-midpoint order2 case even before general superconvergence. Chosen iteration tolerance ||U-U*||<=C h^(p+1) yields collocation order p after accounting for endpoint h F sensitivity; a residual-to-stage inverse bound must convert stopping residual. Spectral node interpolation may have large Lebesgue constants; expose M dependence. No claim of stiff convergence when h L is large; preconditioned scalar linear iteration matrix (I-h lambda Q_delta)^-1 h lambda(Q-Q_delta) is computed and its norm/radius/powers analyzed separately.

**Prerequisites owned here:** node quadrature matrix identity, inverse residual bound, contraction and finite-sweep error, collocation interpolation residual, optional Gauss superconvergence proof. **Examples:** nonstiff high-order IVP, stiff SDC iteration divergence, too-few sweeps dropping order, inexact linear solves. **Cost:** M RHS/stage solves per sweep, reuse of old stage RHS explicitly counted, collocation matrix setup and precision. **Sources, unread candidates:** Dutt/Greengard/Rokhlin, BIT 40 (2000), spectral deferred corrections, https://doi.org/10.1023/A:1022338906936 ; Hairer collocation/RK source https://www.unige.ch/~hairer/poly/chap3.pdf . Exact sections must be read before source acceptance.

amendments.design:
These additions preserve every already approved result. They supply prerequisites locally, without introducing unnecessary pair splits.

- **NA28:** Keep affine mesh/interpolation claims. Add a typed finite oriented cell-complex incidence interface (`boundary boundary=0`), elementwise integration/trace definitions on affine simplices, and reference covariant/contravariant Piola transformations with exact gradient/curl/divergence transformation and normal/tangential moment identities. Prove by affine chain rule, determinant/cofactor identities and cell Green; boundary cancellation uses opposite orientations. Consumers PE08/PE09/PE10. Curved-map approximation remains PE17.
- **NA33:** Preserve SIPG elliptic claims. Its B page may compare with PE04 hyperbolic DG, but no logical claim that elliptic penalty analysis proves nonlinear hyperbolic stability.
- **NA34:** Retain the full existing divergence-lifting/Korn/mini-element binding design. Add an explicitly proved discrete Helmholtz orthogonal projection in the finite velocity mass inner product and pressure Schur-complement identity, including pressure nullspace/gauge. It follows from the already proved inf-sup and finite-dimensional orthogonal decomposition. Used by PE06/PE07; this does not establish bounded-domain Helmholtz regularity.
- **NA35:** Retain reliability/efficiency/contraction/optimality claims and source restrictions. Its conforming refinement algorithm must actually provide the closure, shape-regularity and counting properties it consumes; name newest-vertex bisection initial-label compatibility and dimension. Do not infer 3D mesh complexity from a 2D proof. PE17 is geometric mesh generation/curvature, not a replacement for these obligations.
- **NA36:** Retain full continuous evolution-triple construction. Add the Hilbert-valued discrete energy identity `2(a-b,a)=||a||²-||b||²+||a-b||²` and backward-Euler reconstruction/compactness interface when later used. Aubin–Lions is NOT implicitly supplied: PE12 owns its complete proof and PE06 may consume that supplier.
- **NA38:** Keep the explicit exclusion of an unread second-order pressure-splitting proof. PE07 separately authors an actual first-order projection theorem and separately conditioned higher-order pressure correction.

## Required amendments to the original 46 designs

These are preservation/completion clauses, not permission to erase approved claims.

* **NA-15/17/18:** distinguish absolute stability, positive invariance, conservation and certified adaptive global error. Crosslink XD-03 rather than imply stiff solvers protect nonnegative biological states. Event/history/stiffness extensions remain sibling ownership.
* **NA-22:** particle/symplectic examples must state domain/collision restrictions and actual time-integrator invariants. A Hamiltonian interpretation is a mathematical stipulated model. Neither discrete energy drift plots nor conserved semidiscrete momentum prove a continuum particle limit.
* **NA-23/24/25:** graph/renewal boundary rows are not ordinary rectangular Dirichlet rows. Diffusive L2 stability does not imply positivity; add actual maximum-principle conditions only when proved. Inflow renewal and junction routing go to XD-04/09.
* **NA-26/27:** retain scalar BV entropy scope; it cannot supply multi-species positivity or aggregation/fragmentation moment conservation. The new methods receive independent proofs.
* **NA-28–36:** interval-edge graph trace, renewal inflow trace and particle boundary correction are distinct from simplex H1 trace. Reuse exact established interfaces, supply missing geometry locally. No arbitrary SPH/RBF convergence via Céa unless a real coercive Galerkin structure is proved.
* **NA-39/42:** identify randomness and coupling: particle loading, jump paths, resampling and empirical initial measures differ. Do not transfer independent-level variance proofs to correlated levels or claim N^−1/2 uniform transport error from a scalar MC CLT.
* **NA-43/44/45:** require forward model/sensitivity discretization terms in parameter estimation/design. Identifiability of an exact statistical model does not certify a numerically thresholded Jacobian rank. Preserve approximation, sampling, solver, regularization and model error separately; finite projection/cutoff bias is explicit.

### NA-35 — Adaptive finite-element methods

**Pages:** adaptive-finite-element-methods / adaptive-finite-element-methods-examples.

**Scope:** Define element residuals, normal-flux jumps, data oscillation, Dörfler bulk marking and a conforming refinement algorithm with explicit closure and element-size reduction properties. For the symmetric model problem prove residual reliability, local efficiency up to oscillation, and linear error/oscillation contraction under the source’s assumptions. State optimal complexity only for P₁ Laplace, piecewise-constant data and the declared approximation class; the general coefficient-dependent complexity theorem is not proved in the read source.

**Proof route:** Use Galerkin orthogonality, local interpolation and trace bounds for reliability; bubble functions for local efficiency; prove estimator reduction, quasi-orthogonality and mesh closure before contraction. For nonsymmetric convection carry the source’s sufficiently fine initial-mesh requirement. Separate convergence from optimal work complexity.

**Examples:** Dörfler marking and marked-element refinement; coefficient jump adding oscillation; coarse mesh where nonsymmetric quasi-orthogonality is unavailable.

**Requires:** NA-28 through NA-30; published weak elliptic/Lax–Milgram suppliers and locally proved interpolation/trace estimates.

**Sources:** Nochetto, Adaptive FEM lectures 1–4, complete lectures and PDF/printed pp. 1–47 read: https://www.math.umd.edu/~rhn/lectures/. Lecture 4’s more general coefficient-dependent complexity proof is deferred elsewhere and is not imported; ranges are in fem-spectral/sources.json source_id nochetto-adaptive-fem-lecture-notes-1-to-4.

source_record_verbatim.scope:
genuinely-new finite Gaussian integral algorithms

A: `gaussian-basis-integral-recurrences-and-boys-error`.

Input finitely many Cartesian Gaussian primitives (polynomial times exp(-a|x-A|²), a>0), real centers and contraction coefficients. Define overlap, kinetic, attraction and two-electron Coulomb integrals as mathematical integrals. Prove absolute convergence including Coulomb singularities; Gaussian product theorem by completing squares; polynomial derivative/raising recurrences by differentiation under an explicit integrable dominating function. Reduce Coulomb integrals using 1/r=(2/sqrt(pi)) integral_0^infinity exp(-t²r²)dt with justified Tonelli and a change of variables to Boys F_m(T)=integral_0^1 t^(2m) exp(-Tt²)dt, m>=0,T>=0. Define finite primitive/contracted integral procedure with a declared recurrence ordering, memoization/work model and error budget. Establish Boys Taylor remainder for small T, positive quadrature enclosure on bounded T, and scaled incomplete-gamma/large-T tail bounds. Prove upward/downward recurrence error amplification and domain-based direction switch. Screening skips a block only with a proved bound (e.g. Coulomb Cauchy–Schwarz), and reports total discarded integral/energy bound rather than claiming exact sparsity.

New suppliers owned PC-GINT: Gaussian moment integrals with parameter derivatives; integral representation and recurrence identities; Boys stable-branch error; positive Coulomb bilinear form/Cauchy–Schwarz; tensor contraction error propagation into PC-VAR energy/gradient, with n/r norms explicit. Reuse canonical quadrature and NA01 arithmetic; no HF postulate used. B: same-center s-orbitals exact formula; small-T cancellation in upward recurrence; highly contracted coefficients; overlap near dependence; screening bound accumulated over all discarded blocks. Sources: Obara–Saika recurrence https://doi.org/10.1063/1.450106 ; McMurchie–Davidson https://doi.org/10.1016/0021-9991(78)90092-X ; Helgaker–Jørgensen–Olsen Molecular Electronic-Structure Theory https://doi.org/10.1002/9781119019572 . Reading pending.

source_record_verbatim.scope:
genuinely-new volume scattering computation

A: `volume-integral-scattering-and-partial-wave-error`.

For bounded D in R³ and supplied bounded compactly supported q, define K_k u(x)=integral_D exp(ik|x-y|)/(4pi|x-y|) q(y)u(y)dy on a declared L² or continuous space, k real fixed. Prove boundedness and compactness by truncating the singularity, estimating the discarded small-ball kernel by Schur bounds, and compact approximation of the remaining continuous kernel. For ||K_k||<1 prove Born/Neumann truncation error <=||K_k||^(m+1)||f||/(1-||K_k||). Otherwise existence/stability requires injectivity plus Fredholm (or PDE-owner actual scattering uniqueness under stated q/sign/radiation assumptions). Discretize using PC-NYST-compatible singular product/volume quadrature and prove far-field functional error from the solution estimate and quadrature error. For radial inputs derive the partial-wave radial BVP by explicit spherical harmonic expansion, regular-origin boundary conditions, outer matching and angular-mode truncation bound under a stated coefficient/analyticity regime. Resonance detection uses isolated complex-pole/operator analytic-Fredholm proofs only if fully supplied; a determinant nearly zero is diagnostic, not a theorem.

PC-SCAT owns kernel compactness, volume/far-field maps, radial transform/error; PC-NYST owns discretization spectral clusters; PDE owner owns outgoing uniqueness when actually consumed; linear owner singular quadrature/special transforms; PC-SFUN supplies scaled spherical Bessel evaluations. B: small-norm scatterer Born error; near-resonant amplification; radial square-well comparison with exact matching; forward angular truncation failure at high k unless resolution grows. Sources: Colton–Kress Inverse Acoustic and Electromagnetic Scattering Theory https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-030-30351-8 ; Kress Linear Integral Equations https://doi.org/10.1007/978-1-4614-9593-2 . Reading pending. No unconditional physical scattering model claim.

genuinely-new nonlinear projector iteration, with certified safeguards

A: `self-consistent-projector-iterations-and-certified-mixing`.

Define F(P)=F(P)* and Phi(P)=spectral projector onto the r lowest eigenvalues, only on a declared neighborhood with uniform occupied/unoccupied gap g>0. Define undamped SCF P_{k+1}=Phi(P_k), a distinct relaxed density iteration D_{k+1}=(1-alpha)D_k+alpha Phi(D_k) on a closed admissible Hermitian density set, and a finite-memory DIIS least-squares proposal with singular-system fallback, coefficient/budget cap, and accept/reject rule. Relaxed D is generally not an idempotent projector; keep domains explicit.

Prove block spectral-projector differentiability and Lipschitz bounds from a common separating resolvent contour (or Sylvester off-diagonal equation). If a complete invariant metric neighborhood has Lip(Phi)<=q<1, prove geometric SCF convergence and error<=||P-Phi(P)||/(1-q). For differentiable relaxed map, a certified induced-norm bound ||(1-alpha)I+alpha DPhi||<=q<1 on the whole neighborhood gives the corresponding result. Damping alone is not a proof of contraction. Given inexact Phi evaluations with deterministic error eta_k, prove e_{k+1}<=q e_k+eta_k and the explicit convolution bound. DIIS convergence is claimed only for an actual residual-decreasing safeguarded scheme with a proved contractive baseline and enforceable error budget; bare DIIS gets no universal theorem. Level shifts change the map and require a fixed-point-equivalence proof under their stated eigenvalue ordering.

Full proof route: contour identity and resolvent identity; Weyl gap persistence and uniform inverse estimates; Banach fixed point; telescoping inexact recurrence; accept DIIS only if certified candidate error/residual gives the stipulated contraction, otherwise use baseline. Same-frontier suppliers PC-SCF: block/cluster projector derivative (simple-eigenvalue canonical result is insufficient), computable gap persistence and resolvent bound, level-shift equivalence, safeguard theorem. Generic Anderson acceleration if optimization owner supplies it is reused, not redefined.

B: explicit two-cycle of SCF; zero-gap projector discontinuity; contractive affine response toy model; residual certificate with additive eigensolve tolerance; density mixing leaving the projector manifold; DIIS singular Gram fallback. Candidate sources: Cancès–Le Bris above; Rohwedder–Schneider, DIIS convergence analysis, https://doi.org/10.1007/s00211-011-0401-3 ; Walker–Ni Anderson acceleration, https://doi.org/10.1137/10078356X . Author must inspect exact theorems rather than cite titles as proof.

source_record_verbatim.title: SUPG, residual stabilization and variational multiscale methods
source_record_verbatim.scope: Define SUPG for stationary convection-diffusion-reaction with explicit inflow/boundary conditions, tau_K scaling, diffusion epsilon>0, and c-div(b)/2 bounded below. Prove consistency, coercivity in the stated streamline-diffusion norm and mesh-dependent error bound retaining epsilon/tau/regularity. Define PSPG/grad-div for equal-order flow and prove a concrete stable bilinear norm estimate under a proved pressure stabilization condition. Define VMS as an exact resolved/unresolved algebraic decomposition and one residual closure; a closure/model assertion is not a proven universal turbulence model.
source_record_verbatim.proof_route: Integrate transport by parts with inflow boundary sign; absorb element Laplacian cross terms by NA28 inverse estimate and tau restriction. Bound consistency using the actual residual and interpolate in the stabilized norm. For equal-order pressure control prove the pressure-gradient/local projection lemma and mixed stability; grad-div supplies an additional divergence penalty but does not by itself repair pressure inf-sup. VMS Schur complement follows block elimination; approximation of unresolved inverse has its own defect bound.
source_record_verbatim.examples: convection boundary layer, overlarge stabilization, equal-order pressure oscillation, grad-div pressure sensitivity.

source_record_verbatim.title: Boundary-integral equations and Galerkin BEM
source_record_verbatim.scope: Define single/double-layer potentials, boundary traces/jumps, Calderon operators and Galerkin BEM for 3D Laplace on a closed orientable Lipschitz polyhedral boundary. Prove bounded mappings in H±1/2 trace spaces, correct signed jump identities and ellipticity modulo stated constants/kernel; prove unique stabilized formulation and quasi-optimal error under a shape-regular surface family. Treat 2D logarithmic capacity/scaling separately. Helmholtz combined-field extension consumes PE18 uniqueness and carries frequency-dependent inverse bounds. Quadrature and FMM acceleration have separately controlled matrix perturbation error; they are not free exact BEM.
source_record_verbatim.proof_route: Build Lipschitz trace/lift and dual normal trace, weak layer potentials by variational transmission, then prove singular-kernel representation agrees and derive jumps by transmission/Green. Positivity of single layer from whole-space energy; quotient/gauge removal, Lax–Milgram and NA29 Galerkin. Surface interpolation in fractional norms via a proved local norm/scaling estimate. For Helmholtz use compact perturbation and a locally proved Fredholm alternative plus uniqueness. Kernel principal-value and jump signs are computed, not memorized.
source_record_verbatim.examples: sphere constant density, jump sign orientation, polyhedral singularity, inexact assembly ledger.
source_record_verbatim.missing_prerequisites: :** NA28–30, root fundamental solution/Green/compact operator theory under their actual conditions; own Lipschitz fractional trace/duality/transmission suppliers (published C1 trace is insufficient). Consume linear agent QUAD-SING and LIN-FMM for numerical assembly/acceleration.

source_record_verbatim.title: Compressible viscous flow and entropy-stable viscous fluxes
source_record_verbatim.scope: Define compressible Navier–Stokes–Fourier as a mathematical balance law with positive density/temperature, ideal-gas constitutive functions, nonnegative shear/bulk viscosity and heat conductivity, and specified periodic or entropy-compatible wall boundaries. Derive the continuous entropy identity for smooth positive states. Define a concrete mixed gradient/viscous DG or SBP flux discretization with entropy variables. Prove consistency, global conservation under periodic data and semidiscrete entropy dissipation under the stated positive-semidefinite viscous matrix and boundary flux. Define one finite fully discrete algorithm using the time agent's method; positivity and fully discrete entropy are separate theorems, and may require PE03 limiting plus a proved compatible time discretization. Prove a smooth-solution consistency/error estimate on a compact positive-state tube only when the exact discrete coercivity/linearized stability bound is proved. Do not claim arbitrary-shock or global 3D continuum convergence.
source_record_verbatim.proof_route: Differentiate the mathematical entropy and express viscous flux as K(U) grad(v), deriving symmetry/positive semidefiniteness with its density/temperature factors. Sum local integration by parts, pair the gradient equation with viscous variables, and complete dissipative volume/face squares; compute wall entropy flux explicitly. Interpolate a smooth solution and derive the discrete error identity, controlling nonlinear coefficients by tube bounds, scheme coercivity and Gronwall. Positivity cannot be inferred from entropy dissipation alone; prove the selected limiter/time-step compatibility or retain it as a mandatory unresolved authoring obligation before claiming a fully discrete theorem.
source_record_verbatim.examples: periodic viscous manufactured solution, Couette/thermal wall balance, inviscid-versus-viscous entropy budget, near-vacuum failure.
source_record_verbatim.missing_prerequisites: :** PE01/03/04, NA28/30, PE13 where viscous reconstruction matches; local thermodynamic convexity and viscous entropy-matrix factorization lemmas.

source_record_verbatim.title: First-order least-squares FEM and practical DPG
source_record_verbatim.scope: Define first-order-system least-squares Poisson on H(div)×H1_0 with residual `(sigma+grad u, div sigma-f)` and the correct norm. Prove residual norm equivalent to H(div)×H1_0 error and Galerkin best approximation; boundary conditions are encoded rather than omitted. Define ultraweak Poisson DPG on a stated simplicial mesh with skeleton H1/2 and H-1/2 quotient trace spaces, optimal trial-to-test map via the existing Riesz theorem, and a practical enriched broken test space. Prove continuous inf-sup, ideal energy best approximation, practical quasi-optimality and residual estimator equivalence using a concrete uniformly bounded Fortin operator for the chosen polynomial family/enrichment degree. State the exact degree enrichment from its proved construction. An arbitrary finite test space receives no stability claim.
source_record_verbatim.proof_route: For least-squares recover grad u and sigma from the residual using weak Poisson energy, integration by parts and Poincare; triangle/divergence bounds give both inequalities. For ultraweak form define skeleton norms as minimum-energy extension norms, prove trace surjectivity and extension/lifting without consuming a C1-only boundary theorem on simplices. Prove injectivity/adjoint graph stability and BNB (NA34), then Riesz maps residual to optimal tests. Construct the practical Fortin map locally by moment constraints/bubble corrections, prove polynomial solvability/scaled norm bounds and face trace preservation, then transfer inf-sup. Computed QR/iterative algebraic residual and quadrature perturbations are separately bounded; normal equations still square the matrix condition number under the canonical theorem.
source_record_verbatim.examples: residual certificate for Poisson, omitted boundary residual nonuniqueness, too-small test space, ideal/practical test comparison.
source_record_verbatim.missing_prerequisites: /smallest suppliers:** NA02/28–30/34, PE08/09 weak traces where applicable, `thm-riesz-representation-for-hilbert-space`, existing QR/least-squares results; local skeleton quotient traces/lifts, least-squares graph norm and practical DPG Fortin construction.

source_record_verbatim.title: Reaction-diffusion systems, invariants and pattern computation
source_record_verbatim.scope: Define semilinear vector reaction-diffusion on bounded/periodic domains, quasi-positive reaction, mass conservation/dissipation and invariant rectangles. Prove positivity/invariant-set preservation for a stated mass-lumped FEM or monotone FV diffusion plus a positive reaction step and actual dt bound; prove mass balance. For smooth bounded solutions prove a finite-time error estimate with reaction Lipschitz constants on a common invariant tube. Linearize about a homogeneous equilibrium and derive continuous versus discrete dispersion relations/Turing criterion using the actual discrete Laplacian spectrum. This is linear instability, not existence of nonlinear stable patterns. Crossdiffusion convergence needs a separately stated entropy/coercivity structure, not componentwise maximum principle.
source_record_verbatim.proof_route: M-matrix inverse or convex explicit update, quasi-positive reaction boundary signs, discrete comparison; sum stoichiometric conservation vectors. Error recurrence uses NA36 spatial estimate and time-agent splitting/IMEX with meshuniform operator stability proved for this branch. Fourier/eigenmode diagonalization gives dispersion matrix J-lambda D and its trace/determinant criterion in two species.
source_record_verbatim.examples: Fisher–KPP, activator/inhibitor two-species, finite-grid Turing shift, positivity failure of consistent mass FEM.

source_record_verbatim.title: Exterior waves, absorbing boundaries and PML
source_record_verbatim.scope: Define exterior Helmholtz radiation condition and obstacle boundary data for a specified smooth/Lipschitz obstacle subclass. Prove uniqueness via Rellich identity/outgoing expansion and existence for the chosen combined-field or truncated variational formulation. Define local impedance absorbing boundaries and an exact modal Dirichlet-to-Neumann map for a sphere/circle; prove the actual truncation/reflection error. Define complex-stretch PML first on a Cartesian constant-coefficient mode branch; prove perfect matching and exponential decay there. A finite PML FEM convergence theorem requires the stated obstacle/stretch/parameter stability result and a separate exponential truncation bound; do not universalize the plane-wave calculation to every material or grazing/evanescent mode.
source_record_verbatim.proof_route: Green imaginary part and outgoing expansion prove Rellich uniqueness; combined-field jump relations + Fredholm give existence. Modal separation computes DtN and artificial-boundary reflection. Complex-coordinate substitution computes matching, including branch of longitudinal wave number; bound damping away from the declared excluded angles, then coercive/inf-sup perturbation for truncation and discretization. State Helmholtz pollution restrictions on kh and degree explicitly for any error theorem.
source_record_verbatim.examples: outgoing sphere, impedance reflection, PML normal/grazing incidence, resonance at insufficient damping.
source_record_verbatim.missing_prerequisites: :** NA29/30/38, PE16 layer mappings for the BIE branch; local radiation/Rellich/unique-continuation and PML inf-sup proofs. To avoid cycle, PE16 supplies Laplace/Helmholtz layer mapping without claiming exterior uniqueness; PE18 supplies exterior uniqueness, then a later result homed PE18 proves combined-field solvability consuming PE16.

source_record_verbatim.cycle2_collision_addendum:
### T10/T11 hard-sphere addendum

For finitely many spherical particles with masses m_i>0, radii r_i>0 and smooth external forces on a compact separated configuration tube, define pair guard ||q_i-q_j||-(r_i+r_j). An isolated binary impact has unit normal n=(q_i-q_j)/||q_i-q_j|| and preimpact relative normal velocity v_n=(v_i-v_j) dot n<0. For prescribed restitution e in [0,1], impulse J=-(1+e)v_n/(1/m_i+1/m_j) gives v_i^+=v_i^-+J n/m_i, v_j^+=v_j^--J n/m_j. Prove total linear momentum conservation, normal relative velocity -e v_n and kinetic energy change -(1-e²)v_n²/[2(1/m_i+1/m_j)]. Tangential velocities are unchanged in this frictionless model. These are conditional mathematical collision laws, not a claim that restitution is constant in real materials. Event-driven integration invokes T10 transversality, dense trajectory/guard certificates, event separation, finite event count and restart residual error. Include collision search cost O(P²) naive and any spatial neighbor structure's actual assumptions. Simultaneous collisions, grazing v_n=0, dense frictional multi-contact and inelastic collapse/Zeno violate the isolated binary theorem; return explicit unresolved-event/budget status, or invoke a separately specified complementarity model. T11's scalar complementarity result is not advertised as uniqueness of arbitrary granular frictional contact. A DEM soft-contact penalty is a different ODE model; convergence of penalty to rigid impacts requires its own stiffness/restitution calibration limit and is not inferred from timestep convergence.

source_record_verbatim.scope: Define ALE domain maps with uniformly positive Jacobian, Reynolds transport identity and discrete geometric conservation law; prove free-stream preservation and a conservative scalar transport estimate on a stated moving mesh. Define a linear fluid-structure or diffusion-transmission model with interface continuity and balanced normal flux/traction. Prove monolithic energy balance and a concrete Robin/partitioned time algorithm energy bound under explicit coupling parameters; demonstrate added-mass instability of a specified naive Dirichlet–Neumann recurrence. This is a conditional linear coupling theorem, not general nonlinear FSI well-posedness.
source_record_verbatim.proof_route: Change variables in weak form, differentiate Jacobian using Jacobi's identity and match mesh flux quadrature. Interface terms cancel only for paired trace spaces and signs. Derive coupled block energy, then interface Schur-complement iteration; show contractivity or failure by spectral calculation. Curved interpolation/transfer defects consume PE17, and time-agent splitting contributes a separately bounded splitting residual. Full nonlinear moving-domain convergence needs branch/no-self-intersection and uniform ALE regularity, stated explicitly.

pairs.title: ALE, interfaces and partitioned multiphysics coupling
pairs.scope: Define ALE domain maps with uniformly positive Jacobian, Reynolds transport identity and discrete geometric conservation law; prove free-stream preservation and a conservative scalar transport estimate on a stated moving mesh. Define a linear fluid-structure or diffusion-transmission model with interface continuity and balanced normal flux/traction. Prove monolithic energy balance and a concrete Robin/partitioned time algorithm energy bound under explicit coupling parameters; demonstrate added-mass instability of a specified naive Dirichlet–Neumann recurrence. This is a conditional linear coupling theorem, not general nonlinear FSI well-posedness.
pairs.proof_routes: Change variables in weak form, differentiate Jacobian using Jacobi's identity and match mesh flux quadrature. Interface terms cancel only for paired trace spaces and signs. Derive coupled block energy, then interface Schur-complement iteration; show contractivity or failure by spectral calculation. Curved interpolation/transfer defects consume PE17, and time-agent splitting contributes a separately bounded splitting residual. Full nonlinear moving-domain convergence needs branch/no-self-intersection and uniform ALE regularity, stated explicitly.
pairs.examples: expanding mesh constant state, two-domain heat flux balance, elastic piston added-mass recurrence.

source_record_verbatim.title: hp finite elements and spectral elements
source_record_verbatim.scope: Define conforming variable-degree element spaces on an explicitly admissible matching mesh and polynomial-degree assignment, hierarchical basis, p/h/hp refinement, and a tensor-product Gauss–Lobatto spectral element on affine quadrilaterals/hexahedra. Prove p-explicit local approximation and inverse/trace inequalities, including degree factors in penalties/preconditioners. Derive energy error via NA29 with actual h,p,regularity dependence. Prove exponential p convergence for analytic solutions on a fixed regular mesh using a stated analytic derivative bound. For polygonal corner singularities prove exponential-in-a-power-of-DOF hp convergence only on the explicitly geometrically graded mesh and weighted-analytic regularity class, with the actual grading/degree law. Spectral-element GLL quadrature error is a Strang crime: mass/stiffness norms must be proved equivalent with p-uniform constants in the stated branch; do not equate collocation with exact Galerkin without checking quadrature.
source_record_verbatim.proof_route: Construct reference interval polynomial projection using integrated orthogonal bases and derivative coefficient estimates; tensorize and transport with p-explicit constants. Prove face lifting/conforming assembly for varying degrees. Combine analytic derivative growth and factorial estimates to optimize truncation; for corners sum weighted layer approximation errors and count all DOFs to derive the claimed exponent. GLL norm equivalence and quadrature defects follow exactness plus explicit top-mode correction; variable coefficients require bounded smoothness and aliasing control. Root may select a 2D theorem first, but cannot infer its dimension exponent in 3D.
source_record_verbatim.examples: analytic p refinement, corner singularity h versus hp, GLL mass top mode, p-dependent DG penalty failure.
source_record_verbatim.missing_prerequisites: /smallest suppliers:** NA10/12/28–30/35/38, PE17 for curved extension; local p-explicit polynomial projection/trace/lifting, weighted corner regularity and graded-mesh counting proofs.

source_record_verbatim.title: Isogeometric Galerkin discretization
source_record_verbatim.scope: Reuse canonical B-splines and APP-SPLINE approximation. Define tensor-product rational spline/NURBS geometry with positive weights bounded above/below, globally injective patch map, positive Jacobian and declared derivative/inverse bounds. Define the mapped conforming Galerkin Poisson/linear-elasticity space, h/p/k refinement conventions and compatible multipatch interfaces. Prove weighted rational basis partition/nonnegativity using existing polynomial basis, mapped approximation/stability and a Céa/Strang energy error retaining degree, weight, map and continuity constants. Positive weights do not prove map injectivity. Exact CAD representation does not alone prove exact quadrature or eliminate geometric error for an approximated target. Nonmatching multipatches require a separately stable mortar/Nitsche interface result and are not silently conforming.
source_record_verbatim.proof_route: Quotient derivative formula plus positive denominator gives rational-space norm control; pull back coefficients/energy by PE17 and apply the actual spline quasi-interpolation result to the numerator/comparison space. Prove boundary-preserving projector and interface compatibility; bound rational denominator derivatives and mapping constants explicitly. Apply NA29 for exact geometry/form and NA30 for quadrature/geometry error. h,p,k rates must use the precise spline approximation theorem; no degree-independent condition number from smooth basis alone.
source_record_verbatim.examples: exact quarter-circle geometry with verified map, invalid folded patch despite positive weights, k refinement, multipatch continuity mismatch.

source_record_verbatim.title: Semi-Lagrangian characteristic transport
source_record_verbatim.scope: Define characteristic backtracking plus multilinear/barycentric interpolation for linear nonconservative transport on a periodic box or an explicitly resolved inflow/exit branch. Prove maximum/sup-norm stability for nonnegative partition-of-unity interpolation regardless of displacement-to-cell-size ratio. Prove a smooth-solution global error bound distinguishing characteristic foot error, interpolation defect per step and initial/boundary error: for fixed T, a typical bound is C(dt^q+h^(r+1)/dt) when each backtracking step has O(dt^(q+1)) foot error and interpolation has O(h^(r+1)) defect. State the actual joint mesh/time condition; absence of a classical advective CFL does not eliminate consistency constraints. Define a conservative characteristic-cell overlap method and prove mass conservation/positivity separately; pointwise interpolation is not inherently conservative. High-order interpolation receives its actual operator norm/limiter bound, not automatic L∞ contractivity.
source_record_verbatim.proof_route: Characteristic chain rule plus bounded velocity/state derivatives; prove backtracking map stays admissible and handle periodic wrapping/inflow first-hit. Existing ODE local error controls foot error via solution Lipschitz norm. Interpolation convexity proves sup stability; telescope one-step consistency defects with discrete Gronwall. For conservative remapping use Reynolds/Jacobian mass factors for divergence-form transport, orientation/invertibility and partitioned departure-cell measures, then PE17 overlap conservation. Boundary hitting error requires transversal events or exact exit oracle with declared error; no hidden root solve.
source_record_verbatim.examples: rotation across many cells per step, fixed h/dt consistency loss, nonconservative mass drift, conservative deforming-cell remap.
source_record_verbatim.missing_prerequisites: /smallest suppliers:** `def-linear-transport-equation-and-its-characteristic-flow`, root ODE flow regularity, NA10, P-NUM-ODE-02, PE17, time-agent event/exit contracts; local interpolation operator norm and divergence Jacobian transport.
source_record_verbatim.source_locators: Staniforth–Cote, *Semi-Lagrangian Integration Schemes for Atmospheric Models—A Review*, Monthly Weather Review 119 (1991), 2206–2223, https://doi.org/10.1175/1520-0493(1991)119%3C2206:SLISFA%3E2.0.CO;2 (algorithm context); Falcone–Ferretti, *Semi-Lagrangian Approximation Schemes for Linear and Hamilton–Jacobi Equations* (2014), transport interpolation/trajectory convergence chapters, https://doi.org/10.1137/1.9781611973051. Exact error proof must match the chosen interpolation and flow boundary setup.

source_record_verbatim.title: Monotone Hamilton–Jacobi–Bellman schemes and policy iteration
source_record_verbatim.scope: Define monotone upwind and positive-interpolation semi-Lagrangian schemes for a specified first-order HJ/HJB Cauchy problem, and a discounted stationary Bellman equation on a periodic domain with compact or finite controls and bounded Lipschitz coefficients. Prove monotonicity, L∞ stability, consistency and numerical-scheme-to-viscosity convergence by a full half-relaxed-limit argument using the exact existing first-order comparison class. A control minimization over infinite controls is an explicit oracle or a finite control discretization with its own uniform Hamiltonian error. Define finite-control Howard/policy iteration for the assembled proper M-matrix Bellman system; prove monotone improvement and finite termination with deterministic tie handling/no switch on equal value, or state a separately proved contraction stopping bound. Include a concrete second-order Bellman controlled-diffusion scheme on a monotone diagonal-dominant/wide-stencil branch; prove its comparison/convergence with new second-order viscosity suppliers. No generic central stencil monotonicity for arbitrary anisotropic diffusion, no unproved universal convergence rate.
source_record_verbatim.proof_route: Upwind/positive interpolation makes nodal update order preserving; positive discount gives stationary sup contraction and discrete comparison/unique solution. Finite policy matrices have verified M-matrix inverse positivity; compare successive value solutions, show each strict switch strictly improves at a component and eliminate repeated policies using tie rule, so finite policy space terminates. Derive consistency on smooth test functions including h²/dt interpolation and control-grid error where relevant. To pass numerical limits, choose strict touching test functions, extract near-maximal mesh nodes, apply discrete monotonicity replacing states by test-function values plus contact error, then take limsup/liminf; prove boundary/initial barriers and use continuous comparison to squeeze both limits. The published half-relaxed theorem applies to approximate PDE solutions, so this mesh-node consistency proof is genuinely new. For second order locally define semijets/degenerate ellipticity, prove the required theorem of sums via sup/inf convolution and twice-differentiability arguments (with actual local analytic suppliers), then doubling variables and discount produce comparison; prove Perron/barrier existence or obtain it from convergent discrete approximants. These large but established proofs belong here before their consumers, not a citation to Barles–Souganidis. Restrict a second-order theorem to the coefficient/boundary class for which all those estimates are supplied.
source_record_verbatim.examples: eikonal/HJ kink, discounted control switching, monotone versus nonmonotone stencil, diagonal diffusion Bellman manufactured value, infinite-control quantization.
source_record_verbatim.missing_prerequisites: /smallest suppliers:** NA23/25, PE31, existing first-order viscosity definitions/half-relaxed limits/comparison, canonical linear solves; local mesh touching lemma, discrete comparison/M-matrix, finite-policy monotonicity, control discretization, second-order semijet/theorem-of-sums/comparison/barriers. Choice assumptions follow actual extraction/projection proofs.
